sentences.zh: 隋文帝開皇中，將作大匠宇文愷依《月令》造明堂木樣以獻。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Emperor Wen of Sui, Master of Works Yuwen Kai, following the Monthly Ordinances, made a wooden model of the Bright Hall and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Wendi's Kaihuang reign, Master of Works Yuwen Kai built a wooden Bright Hall model per the Monthly Ordinances and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝令有司于京城安業裏內規兆其地，方欲崇建，而諸儒爭論不定，竟議罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to mark out a site within Anyeli in the capital; they were about to build on a grand scale, but the Confucians debated without settling it, and in the end the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had offices stake a site in Anyeli; as grand construction neared, Ru scholars deadlocked debate and the work was dropped.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，愷復獻明堂木樣並議狀，屬遷都興役，事又不就。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time, Kai again presented a wooden model of the Bright Hall together with a memorial of proposals; it coincided with moving the capital and labor projects, and again the affair did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yangdi, Kai again offered a model and memorial; capital relocation and public works intervened, and again nothing was built.

sentences.zh: 終於隋代，季秋大享，恆在雩壇設祀。

translations.literal: Through the Sui dynasty, the great autumnal offering was always performed with sacrifice set up at the Rain Altar.
translations.idiomatic: For all of Sui, the autumn great offering was always held at the Rain Altar.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，不遑創儀。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he had no leisure to establish ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, taking the mandate, had no time to fix ritual.

sentences.zh: 太宗平定天下，命儒官議其制。

translations.literal: When Taizong pacified the realm, he ordered Confucian officials to deliberate on its form.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong pacified the realm, he ordered Ru officials to debate its design.

sentences.zh: 貞觀五年，太子中允孔穎達以諸儒立議違古，上言曰：「臣伏尋前敕，依禮部尚書盧寬、國子助教劉伯莊等議，以為'從昆侖道上層祭天'。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguan, Palace Companion to the Heir Kong Yingda, [holding that] the various Confucians' proposals violated antiquity, memorialized, saying: 'Your subject humbly searches out the prior edict, following Minister of Rites Lu Kuan, Academician Instructor Liu Bozhuang, and others, who held that one should ascend along the Kunlun Way to the upper level to sacrifice to Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan 5: Palace Companion Kong Yingda, finding Ru proposals unfaithful to antiquity, memorialized that prior edicts, following Lu Kuan and Liu Bozhuang, held sacrifice to Heaven should ascend the Kunlun Way to an upper level.

sentences.zh: 又尋後敕云：'為左右閣道，登樓設祭。

translations.literal: He also searched out a later edict saying: 'Make left and right covered walkways and ascend the tower to set up sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: A later edict likewise required left and right covered walkways and tower sacrifice.

sentences.zh: '臣檢六藝群書百家諸史，皆名基上曰堂，樓上曰觀，未聞重樓之上而有堂名。

translations.literal: 'Your subject has examined the Six Classics, collected books, the hundred schools, and various histories—all name the foundation level hall and the upper level observatory; I have not heard of hall naming above a double-storey structure.'
translations.idiomatic: Classics, histories, and masters all call the base level a hall and the upper an observatory—never a hall atop a double storey.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：'宗祀文王於明堂'。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Honor and sacrifice to King Wen in the Bright Hall.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety honors and sacrifices King Wen in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 不雲明樓、明觀，其義一也。

translations.literal: It does not say Bright Tower or Bright Observatory—the meaning is one.
translations.idiomatic: It does not say Bright Tower or Bright Observatory—the sense is the same.

sentences.zh: 又明堂法天，聖王示儉，或有翦蒿為柱，葺茅作蓋。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Bright Hall models Heaven; sage kings display thrift—sometimes cutting artemisia for pillars and thatching straw for a roof.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall mirrors Heaven; sage kings showed thrift—artemisia pillars, straw roofs.

sentences.zh: 雖復古今異制，不可恆然，猶依大典，惟在樸素。

translations.literal: Though ancient and modern forms differ and cannot remain constant, still following the great canon, only simplicity is fit.
translations.idiomatic: Forms change with age, yet the great canon still demands plainness.

sentences.zh: 是以席惟颭秸，器尚陶匏，用繭栗以貴誠，服大裘以訓儉，今若飛樓架道，綺閣淩雲，考古之文，實堪疑慮。

translations.literal: Thus mats were only winnowed stalks, vessels valued pottery and gourds, cocoon and chestnut used to value sincerity, great fur robes worn to instruct in thrift—now if flying towers span walkways and brocade pavilions pierce the clouds, when one investigates the ancient texts, this is truly subject to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Mats of winnowed stalks, pottery and gourds, cocoon and chestnut for sincerity, great fur for thrift—yet now flying towers, covered walkways, brocade pavilions cloud-high: the ancients would doubt it.

sentences.zh: 按《郊祀志》：漢武明堂之制，四面無壁，上覆以茅。

translations.literal: According to the Monograph on Suburban Sacrifice: Emperor Wu's Bright Hall had four open sides without walls, roofed above with thatch.
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifice monograph: Wu's Bright Hall was open on four sides, thatched above, without walls.

sentences.zh: 祭五帝於上座，祀後土於下防。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors were sacrificed at the upper seat; rear Earth was sacrificed at the lower berm.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors at the upper seat; Earth at the lower berm.

sentences.zh: 臣以上座正為基上，下防惟是基下。

translations.literal: Your subject takes the upper seat as properly on the foundation; the lower berm is solely at the foundation's foot.
translations.idiomatic: The upper seat is the base; the lower berm is its foot—nothing above.

sentences.zh: 既雲無四壁，未審伯莊以何知上層祭神，下有五室？

translations.literal: Since it says no four walls, how does one know that Bo Zhuang sacrifices to spirits on the upper level with five chambers below?
translations.idiomatic: With no four walls, on what basis does Bo Zhuang place spirit sacrifice above and five chambers below?

sentences.zh: 且漢武所為，多用方士之說，違經背正，不可師祖。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Wu of Han did followed much of the masters of methods' teachings, violating the classics and turning from orthodoxy—not to be taken as model.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's work leaned on fangshi lore, against the classics—not a model.

sentences.zh: 又盧寬等議云：上層祭天，下堂布政，欲使人神位別，事不相干。

translations.literal: Moreover, Lu Kuan and others proposed: the upper level sacrifices to Heaven, the lower hall distributes governance—wishing to separate the positions of men and spirits so matters do not interfere.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kuan et al. wanted Heaven above, government below—men and spirits apart.

sentences.zh: 臣以古者敬重大事，與接神相似，是以朝覲祭祀，皆在廟堂，豈有樓上祭祖，樓下視朝？

translations.literal: Your subject considers that in antiquity important affairs were treated with gravity similar to receiving spirits, so audience and sacrifice were all in the temple hall—how could one sacrifice to ancestors on the upper story and hold court below?
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity treated great affairs like spirit reception—audience and sacrifice shared the hall; not sacrifice aloft and court below.

sentences.zh: 閣道升樓，路便窄隘，乘輦則接神不敬，步往則勞勩聖躬。

translations.literal: Covered walkways ascending the tower—the way is narrow and cramped; riding a palanquin then lacks reverence in receiving spirits; going on foot then wearies the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Covered walkways up a tower are cramped—carriage lacks reverence, walking wearies the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 侍衛在旁，百司供奉。

translations.literal: Guards attend at the side; the hundred offices supply service.
translations.idiomatic: Guards flank him; the hundred offices attend.

sentences.zh: 求之典誥，全無此理。

translations.literal: Sought in the canons and ordinances—nowhere is this principle.
translations.idiomatic: Canons and ordinances know nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢固執愚見，以求己長。

translations.literal: Your subject does not presume to cling to a foolish view to seek personal advantage.
translations.idiomatic: I do not cling to my own view for gain.

sentences.zh: 伏以國之大典，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Humbly—the state's great canon cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: The state's great rites demand caution.

sentences.zh: 乞以臣言下群臣詳議。

translations.literal: I beg that my words be sent down to the ministers for detailed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the court to deliberate my words.

sentences.zh: 」侍中魏征議曰：「稽諸古訓，參以舊圖，其上圓下方，復廟重屋，百慮一致，異軫同歸。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Vice Censor Wei Zheng memorialized, saying: "Investigating ancient instructions and comparing with old diagrams, [the form is] round above and square below, compound temple and double roof—all plans agree, different carriages same destination.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Vice Censor Wei Zheng argued: round above, square below, layered temple and double roof—one aim, many paths.

sentences.zh: 洎當塗膺籙，未遑斯禮；

translations.literal: When the House of Cao received the mandate, there was no leisure for this rite;
translations.idiomatic: Cao had the mandate but no time for the rite;

sentences.zh: 典午聿興，無所取則。

translations.literal: when the House of Sima arose, nothing was taken as model.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took no model.

sentences.zh: 裴頠以諸儒持論，異端蜂起，是非舛互，靡所適從，遂乃以人廢言，止為一殿。

translations.literal: Pei Song, because the Confucians held disputations and heterodoxies swarmed like bees, right and wrong crossed and there was nowhere to follow, thereupon discarded men's words and stopped at a single hall.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Song, amid swarming Ru disputes, abandoned debate and built only one hall.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊即仍其舊，梁、陳遵而不改。

translations.literal: Song and Qi continued the old; Liang and Chen followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Qi kept the old form; Liang and Chen unchanged.

sentences.zh: 雖嚴配有所，祭享不匱，求之典則，道實未弘。

translations.literal: Though solemn matching had its place and sacrifices were not lacking, sought in the canonical pattern, the Way was in truth not enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice continued, yet the canonical Way was never fully realized.

sentences.zh: 夫孝因心生，禮緣情立。

translations.literal: Filial piety arises from the heart; ritual is established from feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety springs from the heart; ritual from feeling.

sentences.zh: 心不可極，故備物以表其誠；

translations.literal: The heart cannot be exhausted, so things are prepared to display sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: Hearts cannot be fully shown—objects display sincerity;

sentences.zh: 情無以盡，故飾宮以廣其敬。

translations.literal: feeling cannot be fully expressed, so palaces are adorned to broaden reverence.
translations.idiomatic: feeling cannot be fully expressed—palaces widen reverence.

sentences.zh: 宣尼美意，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: The Master Kong's fine intent lies here!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's intent is here!

sentences.zh: 臣等親奉德音，令參大議，思竭塵露，微增山海。

translations.literal: We your subjects have personally received the virtuous command to join the great deliberation, thinking to exhaust our dust and dew to add slightly to mountain and sea.
translations.idiomatic: We received command to join debate, offering dust to swell mountain and sea.

sentences.zh: 凡聖人有作，義重隨時，萬物斯睹，事資通變。

translations.literal: Whenever the sage makes something, the meaning weighs with the times; all things witness it—the affair depends on adaptation.
translations.idiomatic: Sage works shift with the times; all things witness adaptation.

sentences.zh: 若據蔡邕之說，則至理失于文繁；

translations.literal: If one follows Cai Yong's sayings, then utmost principle is lost in textual excess;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's line loses principle in excess text;

sentences.zh: 若依裴頠所為，則又傷於質略。

translations.literal: if one follows what Pei Song did, then again it injures through plainness and brevity.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Song's line injures through bare plainness.

sentences.zh: 求之情理，未允厥中。

translations.literal: Sought in reason and feeling, it does not satisfy the mean.
translations.idiomatic: Neither satisfies the mean.

sentences.zh: 今之所議，非無用舍。

translations.literal: What is now deliberated is not without use and discard.
translations.idiomatic: Today's debate has real choices.

sentences.zh: 請為五室重屋，上圓下方，既體有則象，又事多故實。

translations.literal: We ask for five chambers in a double roof, round above and square below—both embodying regulated images and grounded in many established facts.
translations.idiomatic: We propose five chambers, double roof, round above and square below—regulated image and solid precedent.

sentences.zh: 下室備布政之居，上堂為祭天之所，人神不雜，禮亦宜之。

translations.literal: The lower chambers prepare dwellings for distributing governance; the upper hall is the place for sacrificing to Heaven—men and spirits not mixed, and the ritual is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Lower chambers for government, upper hall for Heaven—men and spirits apart, ritual fit.

sentences.zh: 其高下廣袤之規，几筵尺丈之制，則並隨時立法，因事制宜。

translations.literal: As for regulations of height, breadth, and extent, and the measures of benches and mats in feet and yards—all follow legislation for the time and suit the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Heights, breadths, benches, and mats should follow the times and the task.

sentences.zh: 自我而作，何必師古。

translations.literal: What we ourselves make—why must we take the ancients as teacher?
translations.idiomatic: Our own work need not ape antiquity.

sentences.zh: 廓千載之疑議，為百王之懿範。

translations.literal: Dispel a thousand years' doubtful debate; be the fine pattern for a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Clear millennial doubt; set a pattern for a hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 不使泰山之下，惟聞黃帝之法；

translations.literal: Do not let below Mount Tai one hear only the Yellow Emperor's law;
translations.idiomatic: Do not leave Mount Tai hearing only the Yellow Emperor;

sentences.zh: 汶水之上，獨稱漢武之圖。

translations.literal: on the Wen River alone praise Wu of Han's plan.
translations.idiomatic: or the Wen River praising only Han Wu.

sentences.zh: 則通乎神明，庶幾可俟，子來經始，成之不日。

translations.literal: Then penetrating to spirits and gods, it may nearly be awaited; the people come and ground is broken—completed not in days.
translations.idiomatic: Then spirits may be reached; the people will come and finish it quickly.

sentences.zh: 」議猶未決。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The deliberation was still undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Debate remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 十七年五月，秘書監顏師古議曰：

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year, Director of the Palace Library Yan Shigu memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth year, fifth month: Palace Library Director Yan Shigu memorialized:

sentences.zh: 明堂之制，爰自古昔，求之簡牘，全文莫睹。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall's form, from ancient times—sought in bamboo and silk, the full text is nowhere seen.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall design is ancient, yet full texts are lost on bamboo and silk.

sentences.zh: 始之黃帝，降及有虞，彌曆夏、殷，迄于周代，各立名號，別創規模。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor down to Shun of Yu, through Xia and Yin to the Zhou age, each established names and separately created models.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through Yu Shun, Xia, Yin, and Zhou—each named and shaped its own form.

sentences.zh: 眾說舛駁，互執所見，巨儒碩學，莫有詳通。

translations.literal: The many sayings contradict; each clings to his view; great Ru and eminent scholars have none who thoroughly penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Sayings clash; great scholars none thorough.

sentences.zh: 斐然成章，不知裁斷。

translations.literal: Floridly formed into chapters, they do not know how to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Fine chapters abound—no decision.

sentences.zh: 究其指要，實布政之宮也。

translations.literal: Investigating the essentials, it is in truth the palace of distributing governance.
translations.idiomatic: At bottom it is the hall of government.

sentences.zh: 徒以戰國縱橫，典籍廢棄；

translations.literal: Only because in the Warring States period strategists crossed and classics were abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Warring States scheming abandoned the classics;

sentences.zh: 暴秦酷烈，經禮湮亡。

translations.literal: violent Qin was cruel and fierce, and classic ritual perished.
translations.idiomatic: cruel Qin extinguished canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 今之所存，傳記雜說，用為准的，理實蕪昧。

translations.literal: What survives today—miscellaneous sayings in transmitted records—used as standard, are in principle muddled and obscure.
translations.idiomatic: What survives—miscellaneous records—is a muddy standard.

sentences.zh: 然《周書》之敘明堂，紀其四面，則有應門、雉門，據此一堂，固是王者之常居耳。

translations.literal: Yet the Zhou Documents' account of the Bright Hall records its four sides, then there are the responding gate and pheasant gate; based on this single hall, it is solidly the Son of Heaven's usual residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhou Documents' Bright Hall lists responding and pheasant gates—one hall, the king's usual dwelling.

sentences.zh: 其青陽、總章、玄堂、太廟及左個、右個，與四時之次相同，則路寢之義，足為明證。

translations.literal: Its Qingyang, Zongzhang, Xuantang, Grand Temple, and left and right annexes, matching the sequence of the four seasons, then the meaning of the road chamber is sufficient as clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyang, Zongzhang, Xuantang, Grand Temple, and left and right annexes match the four seasons—the road chamber is proved.

sentences.zh: 又《文王居明堂》之篇：帶以弓蜀，祠于高禖。

translations.literal: Also the chapter King Wen Dwelling in the Bright Hall: girded with bow Shu, he sacrificed at the high Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen Dwelling in the Bright Hall: girded with bow Shu, he sacrificed at the high Altars of Soil and Grain.

sentences.zh: 下九門磔禳以禦疾疫，置梁除道以利農夫，令國有酒以合三族。

translations.literal: Below the nine gates he dismembered offerings to ward off pestilence, set beams and cleared roads to benefit farmers, and ordered the state to have wine to unite the three clans.
translations.idiomatic: At the nine gates he offered dismemberment against plague, cleared roads for farmers, and ordered state wine for the three clans.

sentences.zh: 」凡此等事，皆合《月令》之文。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." All such affairs accord with the Monthly Ordinances text.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. All match the Monthly Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 觀其所為，皆在路寢者也。

translations.literal: Observing what was done, all was in the road chamber.
translations.idiomatic: All these acts belong in the road chamber.

sentences.zh: 《戴禮》：「昔周公朝諸侯于明堂之位，天子負斧扆南向而立。

translations.literal: The Record of the Elder Dai says: "In former times the Duke of Zhou received the feudal lords at the Bright Hall; the Son of Heaven bore the axe-screen facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Elder Dai: the Duke of Zhou received lords at the Bright Hall; the Son of Heaven bore the axe-screen facing south.

sentences.zh: 明堂也者，明諸侯之尊卑也。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall clarifies the feudal lords' precedence." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall clarifies lords' rank. The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」《周官》又雲「周人明堂，度九尺之筵，東西九筵，堂一筵。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou also says: "The Zhou people's Bright Hall measured the nine-foot bench; east and west nine benches, the hall one bench." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Offices of Zhou: Zhou Bright Hall used a nine-foot bench; nine benches east and west, one bench for the hall. The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」據其制度，即大寢也。

translations.literal: According to its regulations, it is the great chamber.
translations.idiomatic: By its measure it is the great sleeping chamber.

sentences.zh: 《屍子》亦曰：「黃帝曰合宮，有虞氏曰總章，殷曰陽館，周曰明堂。

translations.literal: The Shizi also says: "The Yellow Emperor called it the Harmonious Palace; Shun of Yu called it Zongzhang; Yin called it the Yang Lodge; Zhou called it the Bright Hall." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Shizi: the Yellow Emperor called it Harmonious Palace; Yu Shun Zongzhang; Yin the Yang Lodge; Zhou the Bright Hall. The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」斯皆路寢之征，知非別處。

translations.literal: These are all marks of the road chamber—knowing it is no separate place.
translations.idiomatic: All mark the road chamber—not a separate site.

sentences.zh: 大戴所說，初有近郊之言，復稱文王之廟，進退無據，自為矛盾。

translations.literal: What the Elder Dai said at first had words of proximity to the suburbs, then again called it King Wen's temple—advancing and retreating without warrant, contradicting itself.
translations.idiomatic: Elder Dai first nears the suburbs, then calls it King Wen's temple—self-contradicting.

sentences.zh: 原夫負扆受朝，常居出入，既在皋庫之內，亦何雲於郊野哉？

translations.literal: Considering that bearing the screen to receive audience and usual coming and going were within the outer treasury—how could one say in suburban wilds?
translations.idiomatic: Audience at the screen and daily comings and goings were inside the outer treasury—not suburban wilds.

sentences.zh: 《孝經傳》雲「在國之陽」，又無里數。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety Commentary says "in the yang of the state," again without li count.
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety commentary: "in the state's yang"—no distance given.

sentences.zh: 漢武有懷創造，詢於搢紳，言論紛然，終無定據，乃立于汶水之上而宗祀焉，明其不拘遠近，無擇方面。

translations.literal: Wu of Han cherished creative intent and inquired of the gentry; talk was abundant yet in the end without fixed warrant, and he established it on the Wen River to honor and sacrifice—showing he was not bound by distance or choosy about direction.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wu sought to innovate, asked the gentry, got no fixed answer, and built on the Wen River—distance and direction did not bind him.

sentences.zh: 孝成之代，表行城南，雖有其文，厥功靡立。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Cheng, a memorial proposed the south of the city; though there was text, the achievement was not established.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng proposed south of the city on paper; nothing was built.

sentences.zh: 平帝元始四年，大議營創。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era, great deliberation planned construction.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Yuanshi 4: the court planned construction.

sentences.zh: 孔牢等乃以為明堂、辟雍、太學，其實一也，而有三名。

translations.literal: Kong Lao and others then held that the Bright Hall, Imperial Academy, and Grand Academy were in substance one, yet had three names.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Lao held Bright Hall, Imperial Academy, and Grand Academy were one thing with three names.

sentences.zh: 金褒等又稱經傳無文，不能分別同異。

translations.literal: Jin Bao and others also said the classics and transmitted texts had no writing and could not distinguish sameness and difference.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Bao said the classics lacked text to separate them.

sentences.zh: 中興之後，蔡邕作論，復雲明堂太廟，一物二名。

translations.literal: After the restoration, Cai Yong wrote a treatise, again saying Bright Hall and Grand Temple were one thing, two names.
translations.idiomatic: After restoration Cai Yong wrote: Bright Hall and Grand Temple—one thing, two names.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄則曰：「在國之陽，三里之外。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Zheng Xuan then said: "In the yang of the state, three li outside." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Zheng Xuan: "in the state's yang, three li out." The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」淳於登又云：「三里之外，七里之內，丙巳之地。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Chunyu Deng also said: "Three li outside, seven li within, in the bing-si direction." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Chunyu Deng: "three li out, seven li in, bing-si direction." The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」潁容《釋例》亦云：「明堂太廟，凡有八名，其體一也。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Ying Rong's Explanatory Examples also said: "Bright Hall and Grand Temple have eight names in all; the substance is one." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Ying Rong: "Bright Hall and Grand Temple have eight names; one substance." The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」苟立同異，競為巧說，並出自胸懷，曾無師祖。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." If each sets up sameness and difference and competes in clever explanations—all from the breast, never from teachers and models.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Each clever theory came from the breast, not from masters.

sentences.zh: 審夫功成作樂，理定制禮，草創從宜，質文遞變。

translations.literal: Considering that when achievement is complete music is made and when principle is settled ritual is fashioned—draft creation follows convenience, substance and ornament alternate in change.
translations.idiomatic: Achievement brings music; settled principle brings ritual—drafts follow need, substance and ornament shift.

sentences.zh: 旌旗冠冕，古今不同，律度權衡，前後不一，隨時之義，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Banners, caps, and crowns differ ancient and modern; measures, standards, and balances differ former and later—the meaning of following the time can be known by breaking.
translations.idiomatic: Banners and caps, measures and balances all change with time—plain to see.

sentences.zh: 假如周公舊章，猶當擇其可否；

translations.literal: Suppose even the Duke of Zhou's old statutes—still one should choose what may and may not;
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou Gong's statutes need yes-or-no choices;

sentences.zh: 宣尼彝則，尚或補其闕漏。

translations.literal: the Master Kong's constant pattern—even he sometimes mended its gaps and leaks.
translations.idiomatic: even Confucius's pattern needed patching.

sentences.zh: 況鄭氏臆說，淳于謏聞，匪異守株，何殊膠柱？

translations.literal: How much more Zheng's speculative sayings and Chunyu's shallow hearing—not different from guarding a stump, what different from gluing the peg?
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's guesses and Chunyu's hearsay are stump-guarding and peg-gluing.

sentences.zh: 愚謂不出墉雉，邇接宮闈，實允事宜，諒無所惑。

translations.literal: This foolish one considers: not going beyond the outer wall and pheasant, close to the palace gates—truly fitting the affair, surely without confusion.
translations.idiomatic: I say: within the pheasant wall, beside the palace—fitting and clear.

sentences.zh: 但當上遵天旨，祗奉德音，作皇代之明堂，永貽范于來葉。

translations.literal: Only follow Heaven's command above, reverently receive the virtuous command, make the Bright Hall of the imperial age, and forever bequeath a model to coming generations.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Heaven's command, build the dynasty's Bright Hall, and bequeath a model to posterity.

sentences.zh: 區區碎議，皆略而不論。

translations.literal: Petty fragmentary debate—all passed over without discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Petty debate I pass over.

sentences.zh: 又上表曰：「明堂之制，陛下已發德音，久令詳議。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial, saying: 'As for the Bright Hall's form, Your Majesty has already issued the virtuous command and long ordered detailed deliberation.'
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: Your Majesty has long ordered Bright Hall deliberation.

sentences.zh: 但以學者專固，人人異言，損益不同，是非莫定。

translations.literal: Only because scholars are obstinate, each man has a different saying, increase and decrease differ, and right and wrong are not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars are obstinate—each voice differs, nothing settles.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為五帝之後，兩漢已前，高下方圓，皆不相襲。

translations.literal: Your subject's foolish view is that after the Five Emperors and before the two Han dynasties, round above and square below were never alike in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Emperors through pre-Han times, round-above-square-below never repeated.

sentences.zh: 惟在陛下聖情創造，即為大唐明堂，足以傳於萬代，何必論戶牖之多少，疑階庭之廣狹？

translations.literal: Only in Your Majesty's sage intent to create lies the Great Tang Bright Hall, sufficient to transmit through ten thousand generations—why debate how many doors and windows, or doubt the courtyard's breadth and narrowness?
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty's creation need be Tang's Bright Hall for ten thousand generations—why count doors or doubt the courtyard?

sentences.zh: 若恣儒者互說一端，久無斷決，徒稽盛禮，昔漢武欲草封禪儀，博望諸生，所說不同，莫知孰是。

translations.literal: If one lets the Confucians each argue one corner, long without decisive break, one only delays the great rite; formerly when Han Wu wished to draft the fengshan ceremony, the many students of the Broad Vision had different sayings and none knew which was right.
translations.idiomatic: Let Ru argue forever and the great rite stalls; Han Wu drafting fengshan heard many students, none right.

sentences.zh: 唯御史大夫倪寬勸上自定制度，遂成登封之禮。

translations.literal: Only Censor-in-Chief Ni Kuan urged the emperor to fix the system himself, and thereupon the ascent-feng rite was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Censor-in-Chief Ni Kuan urged the emperor to fix the rite himself—and fengshan was done.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚誠，亦望陛下斟酌繁省，為其節文，不可謙拒，以淹大典。

translations.literal: Your subject's foolish sincerity also hopes Your Majesty will weigh fullness and spareness and set its abbreviated text, and cannot decline out of modesty thereby drowning the great canon. The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will trim the text and not decline modesty into delay of the great rite. The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」尋以有事遼海，未暇營創。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of affairs in Liaohai, there was no leisure to plan construction.
translations.idiomatic: Liaohai affairs left no time to build.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年七月二日，敕曰：「上玄幽贊，崇高而不言；

translations.literal: On the second day of the seventh month of the second year of Yonghui, an edict said: "The High Mystery secretly assists, lofty and without speech;
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui 2.7.2—edict: "High Mystery assists in silence;

sentences.zh: 皇王提象，代神功而理物。

translations.literal: the imperial king grasps the image, replacing divine achievement to order things.
translations.idiomatic: the king grasps the image, ordering things in Heaven's stead.

sentences.zh: 是知五精降德，爰應帝者之尊；

translations.literal: Thus one knows the five essences descend virtue and respond to the emperor's honor;
translations.idiomatic: five essences descend virtue to the emperor;

sentences.zh: 九室垂文，用紀處天之業。

translations.literal: the nine chambers hang text, used to record the work of residing in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: nine chambers record the work of dwelling in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 且合宮、靈府，創鴻規於上代；

translations.literal: Moreover Harmonious Palace and Spirit Storehouse created great models in high antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious Palace and Spirit Storehouse set high antiquity's models;

sentences.zh: 太室、總章，標茂范於中葉。

translations.literal: Grand Chamber and Zongzhang marked flourishing patterns in the middle age.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chamber and Zongzhang marked the middle age.

sentences.zh: 雖質文殊制，奢儉異時，然其立天中，作人極，布政施教，其歸一揆。

translations.literal: Though substance and text differed in form and extravagance and thrift differed in time, yet establishing the center of Heaven and making the human pole, distributing governance and teaching—their return is one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Forms differed, thrift and splendor shifted—yet center of Heaven, human pole, and teaching were one aim.

sentences.zh: 朕嗣膺下武，丕承上烈，思所以答眷上靈，聿遵孝享，而法宮曠禮，明堂寢構。

translations.literal: We have succeeded to martial achievement and greatly inherited the upper blaze, thinking how to answer the favor of the upper spirit and reverently follow filial offering—yet the ritual palace lacks rites and the Bright Hall sleeps in structure.
translations.idiomatic: We inherited martial glory yet the ritual palace lacks rites and the Bright Hall stands unfinished.

sentences.zh: 今國家四表無虞，人和歲稔，作範垂訓，今也其時。

translations.literal: Now the state's four quarters are without care, men are harmonious and years abundant—establishing pattern and bequeathing instruction, now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is calm and harvest full—now is the time to set pattern.

sentences.zh: 宜令所司與禮官學士等考核故事，詳議得失，務依典禮，造立明堂。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the relevant offices together with ritual officials and academicians to examine precedents, deliberate gain and loss in detail, and with all effort follow canonical ritual to establish the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Let offices and Ru scholars examine precedents, weigh gain and loss, and build the Bright Hall by canonical ritual.

sentences.zh: 庶曠代闕文，獲申於茲日；

translations.literal: May a text missing through the ages find expression on this day;
translations.idiomatic: May ages' missing text find voice today;

sentences.zh: 因心展敬，永垂於後昆。

translations.literal: following the heart to display reverence, forever bequeathed to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: heartfelt reverence bequeathed to posterity.

sentences.zh: 其明堂制度，令諸曹尚書及左右丞侍郎、太常、國子秘書官、弘文館學士同共詳議。

translations.literal: As for the Bright Hall's regulations, order the various department ministers and left and right assistant ministers and vice ministers, the Minister of Rites, Palace Library officials, and Hongwen Pavilion academicians jointly to deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall rules: ministers, vice ministers, Rites, Palace Library, and Hongwen scholars shall deliberate together.

translations.literal: The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 於是太常博士柳宣仍鄭玄義，以為明堂之制，當為五室。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Scholar of the Minister of Rites Liu Xuan still followed Zheng Xuan's meaning, holding that the Bright Hall's form should have five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Rites scholar Liu Xuan held Zheng Xuan's five chambers.

sentences.zh: 內直丞孔志約據《大戴禮》及盧植、蔡邕等義，以為九室。

translations.literal: Inner Rectifier Assistant Kong Zhiyue followed the Elder Dai Rites and Lu Zhi, Cai Yong, and others, holding nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Rectifier Kong Zhiyue, following Elder Dai, Lu Zhi, and Cai Yong, held nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 曹王友趙慈皓、秘書郎薛文思等各造明堂圖。

translations.literal: Friend to the Prince of Cao Zhao Cihao, Secretariat Gentleman Xue Wensi, and others each made Bright Hall diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Cihao, Xue Wensi, and others each drew Bright Hall plans.

sentences.zh: 諸儒紛爭，互有不同。

translations.literal: The Confucians disputed, each differing.
translations.idiomatic: Ru scholars clashed.

sentences.zh: 上初以九室之議為是，乃令所司詳定形制及辟雍門闕等。

translations.literal: At first the emperor took the nine-chamber proposal as right and ordered the relevant offices to fix in detail the form and measures and the Imperial Academy gates and towers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first favored nine chambers and ordered form, gates, and towers fixed.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，內出九室樣，仍更令有司損益之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year, a nine-chamber model was issued from within, and again the relevant offices were ordered to increase or decrease it.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, sixth month: an inner nine-chamber model was issued for revision.

sentences.zh: 有司奏言：

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Offices reported:

sentences.zh: 內樣：堂基三重，每基階各十二。

translations.literal: Inner model: the hall foundation triple-tiered, each foundation twelve steps per tier.
translations.idiomatic: Inner model: triple foundation, twelve steps per tier.

sentences.zh: 上基方九雉，八角，高一尺。

translations.literal: Upper foundation square nine zhi, eight corners, one foot high.
translations.idiomatic: Upper tier: nine zhi square, eight corners, one foot high.

sentences.zh: 中基方三百尺，高一筵。

translations.literal: Middle foundation square three hundred feet, one bench high.
translations.idiomatic: Middle tier: three hundred feet square, one bench high.

sentences.zh: 下基方三百六十尺，高一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Lower foundation square three hundred sixty feet, one zhang two feet high.
translations.idiomatic: Lower tier: three hundred sixty feet square, one zhang two feet high.

sentences.zh: 上基象黃琮，為八角，四面安十二階。

translations.literal: The upper foundation images the yellow jade tube, made eight-cornered; on four sides twelve steps were set.
translations.idiomatic: Upper tier images the yellow tube, eight-cornered, twelve steps on four sides.

sentences.zh: 請從內樣為定。

translations.literal: We ask to take the inner model as fixed.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to fix the inner model.

sentences.zh: 基高下仍請准周制高九尺，其方共作司約准一百四十八尺。

translations.literal: For foundation height we still ask to follow Zhou regulation of nine feet high; its square altogether to follow the Secretariat standard of one hundred forty-eight feet.
translations.idiomatic: Height should follow Zhou's nine feet; square, the Secretariat standard of one hundred forty-eight feet.

sentences.zh: 中基下基，望並不用。

translations.literal: Middle and lower foundations—we hope both unused.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and lower tiers should be dropped.

sentences.zh: 又內樣：室各方三筵，開四闥、八窗。

translations.literal: Also inner model: each chamber square three benches, opening four doors and eight windows.
translations.idiomatic: Inner model: each chamber three benches square, four doors and eight windows.

sentences.zh: 屋圓楣徑二百九十一尺。

translations.literal: The roof's round beam diameter two hundred ninety-one feet.
translations.idiomatic: Round roof-beam diameter: two hundred ninety-one feet.

sentences.zh: 按季秋大饗五帝，各在一室，商量不便，請依兩漢季秋合饗，總於太室。

translations.literal: According to the autumn great offering to the Five Emperors, each in one chamber—deliberation finds it inconvenient; we ask to follow the two Han autumn joint offering, gathering all in the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn offering to the Five Emperors in separate chambers is awkward—we follow two Han practice: one joint rite in the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 若四時迎氣之祀，則各于其方之室。

translations.literal: If it is sacrifice to welcome the qi of the four seasons, then each in its directional chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal qi rites stay in their directional chambers.

sentences.zh: 其安置九室之制，增損明堂故事，三三相重。

translations.literal: As for arranging the nine chambers, increasing and decreasing Bright Hall precedent—three and three layered.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chambers should revise precedent in threes, layered three by three.

sentences.zh: 太室在中央，方六丈。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamber in the center, square six zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chamber center: six zhang square.

sentences.zh: 其四隅之室，謂之左右房，各方二丈四尺。

translations.literal: The four corner chambers are called left and right rooms, each square two zhang four feet.
translations.idiomatic: Four corners: left and right rooms, each two zhang four feet square.

sentences.zh: 當太室四面，青陽、明堂、總章、玄堂等室，各長六丈，以應太室；

translations.literal: Facing the Grand Chamber on four sides, Qingyang, Bright Hall, Zongzhang, Xuantang, and other chambers, each six zhang long to correspond to the Grand Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: On four sides of the Grand Chamber: Qingyang, Bright Hall, Zongzhang, Xuantang—each six zhang long to match the center;

sentences.zh: 闊二丈四尺，以應左右房。

translations.literal: two zhang four feet wide to correspond to the left and right rooms.
translations.idiomatic: two zhang four feet wide to match the corner rooms.

sentences.zh: 室間並通巷，各廣一丈八尺。

translations.literal: Between chambers all connecting lanes, each one zhang eight feet wide.
translations.idiomatic: Connecting lanes between chambers, each one zhang eight feet wide.

sentences.zh: 其九室並巷在堂上，總方一百四十四尺，法坤之策。

translations.literal: The nine chambers and lanes together on the hall, total square one hundred forty-four feet, matching Kun's counting rods.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chambers and lanes atop the hall: one hundred forty-four feet square—Kun's number.

sentences.zh: 屋圓楣、楯、簷，或為未允。

translations.literal: Round roof-beam, balustrade, and eaves—or not yet approved.
translations.idiomatic: Round beam, balustrade, and eaves remain unsettled.

sentences.zh: 請據鄭玄、盧植等說，以前梁為楣，其徑二百一十六尺，法乾之策。

translations.literal: We ask to follow Zheng Xuan, Lu Zhi, and others, taking the front beam as the beam; its diameter two hundred sixteen feet, matching Qian's counting rods.
translations.idiomatic: Per Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi: front beam as main beam, diameter two hundred sixteen feet—Qian's number.

sentences.zh: 圓柱旁出九室四隅，各七尺，法天以七紀。

translations.literal: Round pillars projecting beside the nine chambers at the four corners, each seven feet, matching Heaven's reckoning by seven.
translations.idiomatic: Round pillars at the four corners, seven feet each—Heaven's seven.

sentences.zh: 柱外餘基，節作司約准面別各餘一丈一尺。

translations.literal: Outside the pillars, remaining foundation—section making Secretariat standard; on each face separately one zhang one foot remaining.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the pillars, each face leaves one zhang one foot by Secretariat measure.

sentences.zh: 內樣：室別四闥、八窗，檢與古同，請依為定。

translations.literal: Inner model: each chamber separately four doors and eight windows—checked against antiquity, the same; we ask to fix by this.
translations.idiomatic: Inner model's four doors and eight windows match antiquity—we fix them.

sentences.zh: 其戶依古外設而不開。

translations.literal: The doors, following antiquity, are set outside but not opened.
translations.idiomatic: Doors, per antiquity, are set outside but not opened.

sentences.zh: 內樣：外有柱三十六，每柱十梁。

translations.literal: Inner model: outside thirty-six pillars, ten beams per pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Inner model: thirty-six outer pillars, ten beams each.

sentences.zh: 內有七間，柱根以上至梁高三丈，梁以上至屋峻起，計高八十一尺。

translations.literal: Inside seven bays; from pillar root up to beam three zhang, from beam up to roof ridge rising, total height eight zhang one foot.
translations.idiomatic: Seven inner bays; pillar to beam three zhang; beam to ridge—total eight zhang one foot.

sentences.zh: 上圓下方，飛簷應規，請依內樣為定。

translations.literal: Round above and square below, flying eaves matching compass—we ask to fix by the inner model.
translations.idiomatic: Round above, square below, flying eaves on compass—we fix the inner model.

sentences.zh: 其屋蓋形制，仍望據《考工記》改為四阿，並依禮加重簷，准太廟安鴟尾。

translations.literal: As for the roof-cover form, still we hope to follow the Record of Crafts and change to four slopes, and according to ritual add double eaves, following the Grand Temple in setting owl-tail ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Roof form: follow Crafts for four slopes, double eaves, and Grand Temple owl-tails.

sentences.zh: 堂四向五色，請依《周禮》白盛為便。

translations.literal: The hall's four directions in five colors—we ask to follow the Zhou Rites' white fill as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Four directions, five colors—we follow Zhou white fill.

sentences.zh: 其四向各隨方色。

translations.literal: Each direction follows its directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Each direction takes its color.

sentences.zh: 請施四垣及四門。

translations.literal: We ask to set four enclosing walls and four gates.
translations.idiomatic: We ask four walls and four gates.

sentences.zh: 辟雍，按《大戴禮》及前代說，辟雍多無水廣、內徑之數。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy: according to the Elder Dai Rites and former-age sayings, the Imperial Academy often lacks numbers for water breadth and inner diameter.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy: Elder Dai and older sources often omit water breadth and inner diameter.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕云：「水廣二十四丈，四周於外。

translations.literal: Cai Yong said: "The water twenty-four zhang broad, encircling on the outside." The passage concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong: "water twenty-four zhang wide, encircling outside." The quote ended.

sentences.zh: 」《三輔黃圖》雲「水廣四周」，與蔡邕不異，仍雲「水外周堤」。

translations.literal: The Chart of the Three Metropolises says "water broad on four sides," not differing from Cai Yong, and again says "outside the water a circular embankment."
translations.idiomatic: Three Metropolises Chart: "water on four sides," like Cai Yong, with a circular embankment outside.

sentences.zh: 又張衡《東京賦》稱「造舟為梁」。

translations.literal: Also Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital says 'making boats into a bridge.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Eastern Capital rhapsody speaks of boats as a bridge.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·明堂位》、《陰陽錄》云：「水左旋以象天。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites "Positions in the Bright Hall" and the Yin-Yang Record say: "The water turns left to image Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Rites "Bright Hall Positions" and Yin-Yang Record: "water turns left to mirror Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」商量水廣二十四丈，恐傷於闊，今請減為二十四步，垣外量取周足。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Deliberation finds water twenty-four zhang perhaps too broad; now we ask to reduce to twenty-four paces, measuring the perimeter outside the wall as sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Twenty-four zhang may be too wide—we reduce to twenty-four paces, perimeter measured outside the wall.

sentences.zh: 仍依故事造舟為梁，其外周以圓堤，並取《陰陽》「水行左旋」之制。

translations.literal: Still following precedent to make boats into a bridge; outside, encircle with a round embankment, and take the Yin-Yang system's 'water moves, turning left.'
translations.idiomatic: Keep the boat-bridge precedent, round embankment outside, and left-turning water per Yin-Yang.

sentences.zh: 殿垣，按《三輔黃圖》，殿垣四周方在水內，高不蔽日，殿門去殿七十二步。

translations.literal: Hall wall: according to the Chart of the Three Metropolises, the hall wall on four sides square within the water, high enough not to block the sun; the hall gate seventy-two paces from the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hall wall per Three Metropolises Chart: square within the water, low enough for sun; hall gate seventy-two paces off.

sentences.zh: 准今行事陳設，猶恐窄小。

translations.literal: Compared with present practice for array and setting, it still seems narrow and small.
translations.idiomatic: Present array practice still seems cramped.

sentences.zh: 其方垣四門去堂步數，請准太廟南門去廟基遠近為制。

translations.literal: For the square wall's four gates' distance in paces from the hall, we ask to follow the Grand Temple south gate's distance from the temple foundation as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Gate distances should follow Grand Temple south-gate spacing.

sentences.zh: 仍立四門八觀，依太廟門別各安三門，施玄閫，四角造三重魏闕。

translations.literal: Still establish four gates and eight towers; following the Grand Temple, on each gate side set three gates, install dark lattices, and at the four corners make triple-tier Wei towers.
translations.idiomatic: Four gates, eight towers; three gates each like Grand Temple, dark lattices, triple Wei towers at corners.

sentences.zh: 此後群儒紛競，各執異議。

translations.literal: After this the Confucians disputed competitively, each clinging to a different opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Ru scholars then disputed, each clinging to his view.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射于志寧等請為九室，太常博士唐等請為五室。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yu Zhining and others asked for nine chambers; Palace Scholar of the Minister of Rites Tang and others asked for five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining urged nine chambers; Tang of the Minister of Rites urged five.

sentences.zh: 高宗令於觀德殿依兩議張設，親與公卿觀之。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered both proposals set up in Guande Hall for the emperor personally to view with the dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong had both models set in Guande Hall for the emperor and ministers to view.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「明堂之禮，自古有之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Bright Hall ritual exists from antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Bright Hall rites are ancient."

sentences.zh: 議者不同，未果營建。

translations.literal: Deliberators differed, and construction was not accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Debates differed; nothing was built.

sentences.zh: 今設兩議，公等以何者為宜？

translations.literal: Now setting up the two proposals—which do you, lords, find fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Now two models are shown—which suits you?

sentences.zh: 」工部尚書閻立德對曰：「兩議不同，俱有典故。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Minister of Works Yan Lide replied: "The two proposals differ, each with canonical precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. Minister of Works Yan Lide said: "Both have precedent."

sentences.zh: 九室似暗，五室似明。

translations.literal: Nine chambers seem dim; five chambers seem bright.
translations.idiomatic: Nine chambers seem dim; five seem bright.

sentences.zh: 取捨之宜，斷在聖慮。

translations.literal: What is fitting to take or discard rests in the sacred deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The choice rests with Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上以五室為便，議又不定，由是且止。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." The emperor took five chambers as convenient, yet deliberation was again unsettled, and thereby it was for the time stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. The emperor favored five chambers, debate stalled again, and work paused.

sentences.zh: 至乾封二年二月，詳宜略定，乃下詔曰：「朕以寡薄，忝承丕緒。

translations.literal: By the second month of the second year of Qianfeng, the detailed plan was roughly settled, and an edict was issued:
translations.idiomatic: Qianfeng 2.2: the plan was roughly set and an edict issued:

sentences.zh: 奉二聖之遺訓，撫億兆以初臨，馭朽兢懷，推溝在念。

translations.literal: We, meager and slight, humbly inherit the great succession, uphold the two sages' entrusted instruction, soothe the hundred millions at first assuming rule, hold rotten wood in fearful care, and push the ditch in thought.
translations.idiomatic: We are slight, inheriting the great line, holding the two sages' charge, soothing the millions, fearful on rotten wood, mindful of the ditch.

sentences.zh: 而上玄垂祐，宗社降休，歲稔時和，人殷俗阜。

translations.literal: Yet the High Mystery bestows protection; the altars of the ancestral temple send blessing; years are abundant and seasons harmonious, men numerous and custom rich.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven protects; the altars bless; harvests are full and customs rich.

sentences.zh: 車書混一，文軌大同。

translations.literal: Carriage and writing are unified; culture and tracks are greatly alike.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage script is one; culture and law align.

sentences.zh: 檢玉泥金，升中告禪，百蠻執贄，萬國來庭，朝野俱娛，華夷胥悅。

translations.literal: Inspecting jade and sealing gold, ascending the center and announcing shan, the hundred barbarians present tribute, ten thousand states come to court, court and wilds alike rejoice, Chinese and foreigners all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jade inspected, gold sealed, fengshan announced—barbarians tribute, states at court, all rejoice.

sentences.zh: 但為郊禋嚴配，未安太室，布政施行，猶闕合宮。

translations.literal: Yet for suburban and temple solemn matching, the Grand Chamber is not settled; distributing governance and implementing teaching still lacks the Harmonious Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet suburban matching lacks the Grand Chamber; government and teaching lack the Harmonious Palace.

sentences.zh: 朕所以日昃忘疲，中宵輟寢，討論墳籍，錯綜群言，采三代之精微，探九皇之至賾，斟酌前載，製造明堂。

translations.literal: We therefore from sun tilting forget fatigue, at midnight cease sleep, discuss tomb classics and weave together the many sayings, gather the essence of the three ages and probe the utmost profundity of the nine sovereigns, weigh former records, and fashion the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: So we toil past sunset, study classics, weave debate, gather three ages' essence, and design the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 棟宇方圓之規，雖兼故實；

translations.literal: Though the rules of beams and compass for square and round draw on old facts;
translations.idiomatic: Beam and compass rules draw on old facts;

sentences.zh: 度筵陳俎之法，獨運財成。

translations.literal: the method of measuring benches and setting offerings alone applies financial completion.
translations.idiomatic: bench and offering measures are our own invention.

sentences.zh: 宣諸內外，博考詳議，求其長短，冀廣異聞。

translations.literal: Announce within and without, broadly examine and deliberate in detail, seek strengths and weaknesses, hoping to broaden divergent hearing.
translations.idiomatic: We announce it widely for debate, seeking strengths and broader hearing.

sentences.zh: 而鴻生碩儒，俱稱盡善，搢紳士子，並奏該通。

translations.literal: Yet great-born eminent Ru all called it perfect; gentry and scholars all memorialized thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Great scholars called it perfect; gentry said it was thorough.

sentences.zh: 創此宏模，自我作古。

translations.literal: Creating this great model—we ourselves make antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This great model—we make our own antiquity.

sentences.zh: 因心既展，情禮獲伸，永言宗祀，良深感慰。

translations.literal: Following the heart already displayed, feeling and ritual obtained extension; speaking forever of ancestral sacrifice, truly deep grateful relief.
translations.idiomatic: Heart shown, ritual restored; ancestral rites deeply comfort us.

sentences.zh: 宜命有司，及時起作，務從折中，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the relevant offices timely to commence work, with all effort following the mean, matching our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let offices build at once, following the mean as we intend.

sentences.zh: 」於是大赦天下，改元為總章，分萬年置明堂縣。

translations.literal: The passage concluded." Thereupon a great amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven, the era name changed to Zongzhang, and from Wannian was set apart Bright Hall County.
translations.idiomatic: The quote ended. A great amnesty followed, the era became Zongzhang, and Bright Hall County was split from Wannian.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，又具規制廣狹，下詔曰：

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, the regulations of breadth and narrowness were again fully set, and an edict was issued:
translations.idiomatic: Next year, third month: dimensions were fixed again by edict:

sentences.zh: 合宮聽朔，闡皇軒之茂範；

translations.literal: The Harmonious Palace hears the new moon, opening the flourishing pattern of Yellow Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious Palace at new moon opens Yellow Xuan's pattern;

sentences.zh: 靈府通和，敷帝勳之景化。

translations.literal: the Spirit Storehouse communicates harmony, spreading the emperor's merit and bright transformation.
translations.idiomatic: the Spirit Storehouse harmonizes, spreading imperial merit.

sentences.zh: 殷人陽館，青珪備禮；

translations.literal: The Yin people's Yang Lodge prepared green jade tablets for ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Yin's Yang Lodge set green jade for ritual;

sentences.zh: 姬氏玄堂，彤璋合獻。

translations.literal: the Ji clan's Xuantang combined red tablets in offering.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's Xuantang offered red tablets.

sentences.zh: 雖運殊驪翰，時變質文，至於立天中，建皇極，軌物施教，其歸一揆。

translations.literal: Though fortune differed like black horse and white horse, times changed substance and ornament, yet establishing the center of Heaven and building the imperial pole, tracking things and teaching—their return is one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunes and forms changed, yet Heaven's center, the imperial pole, and teaching were one.

sentences.zh: 考圖汶上，僅存公玉之儀；

translations.literal: Examining the chart on the Wen, barely surviving was Gongyu's ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: Wen River charts barely preserve Gongyu's rite;

sentences.zh: 度室圭躔，才紀中元之制。

translations.literal: measuring the chamber and jade pacing, only the Zhongyuan system was recorded.
translations.idiomatic: chamber and jade measures record only Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 屬炎精墜駕，睿宮毀籥，四海淪於沸鼎，九土陷於塗原。

translations.literal: It happened that the fiery essence fell from its chariot, the wise palace destroyed its pipes; the four seas sank in a boiling cauldron, the nine lands fell into a mud plain.
translations.idiomatic: The Han fiery essence fell, the wise palace's pipes were ruined; seas boiled, lands sank to mud.

sentences.zh: 高祖太武皇帝杖鉞唐郊，收鈐雍野，納祥符于蒼水，受靈命於丕山。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, the Grand Martial Emperor, leaned on his staff at the Tang suburb, gathered the seals of Yong and Ye, received auspicious talismans at the Cang River, and received the numinous mandate at Mount Pi.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor, the Grand Martial Emperor, took the field at Tang’s outskirts, gathered the seals of Yong and Ye, received auspicious talismans at the Cang River, and received the numinous mandate at Mount Pi.

sentences.zh: 飛沈泳沫，動植遊源。

translations.literal: What sinks and floats, swims in foam—moving things and plants all find their source.
translations.idiomatic: All that sink or float, all moving things and plants, drew life from that source.

sentences.zh: 太宗文皇帝盟津光誓，協降火而登壇；

translations.literal: The Literary Emperor Taizong made a bright oath at Meng Ford and joined in descending the fire to ascend the altar;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, the Literary Emperor, swore a bright oath at Meng Ford and, joining the descent of fire, ascended the altar;

sentences.zh: 豐谷斷蛇，應屯雲而鞠旅。

translations.literal: at Feng Valley he cut the serpent and, responding to massed clouds, mustered his hosts.
translations.idiomatic: at Feng Valley he cut the serpent and, as clouds gathered, mustered his hosts.

sentences.zh: 封金貸嶺，昭累聖之鴻勳；

translations.literal: He enfeoffed at Golden Loan Ridge and displayed the great merit of successive sages;
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed at Golden Loan Ridge and proclaimed the accumulated merit of the sage line;

sentences.zh: 勒石丸都，成文考之先志。

translations.literal: he carved stone at Wandu and fulfilled his father’s earlier intent.
translations.idiomatic: he carved stone at Wandu and carried out his father’s long-held plan.

sentences.zh: 固可以作化明堂，顯庸太室。

translations.literal: Thus they could transform through the Bright Hall and display merit in the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they could transform the realm through the Bright Hall and display merit in the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 傍羅八柱，周建四門，木工不琢，土事無文，豐約折衷，經始勿亟，闕文斯備，大禮聿修。

translations.literal: They arrayed eight pillars on the sides and built four gates all around; carpentry needed no carving, earthworks no ornament—abundance and restraint were balanced, beginning was not rushed, what was lacking in pattern was made complete, and the great rites were thereupon perfected.
translations.idiomatic: They arrayed eight pillars and built four gates all around; carpentry needed no carving and earthworks no ornament—abundance and restraint were balanced, the work was not rushed, pattern was completed where it had been lacking, and the great rites were perfected.

sentences.zh: 其明堂院每面三百六十步，當中置堂。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall precinct was three hundred sixty paces on each face, with a hall placed in the center.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall precinct measured three hundred sixty paces on each side, with a hall at the center.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策一百四十有四，總成三百六十，故方三百六十步。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, the Qian tally is two hundred sixteen and the Kun tally one hundred forty-four, totaling three hundred sixty; therefore each face was three hundred sixty paces.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes gives Qian’s tally as two hundred sixteen and Kun’s as one hundred forty-four—three hundred sixty in all—so each face was made three hundred sixty paces.

sentences.zh: 當中置堂，處二儀之中，定三才之本，構茲一宇，臨此萬方。

translations.literal: A hall was placed in the center, standing between the Two Modes and fixing the root of the Three Powers, constructing this one hall to oversee the ten thousand regions.
translations.idiomatic: The central hall stood between Heaven and Earth, fixed the root of the Three Powers, and from this single structure looked out over the realm.

sentences.zh: 自降院每面三門，同為一宇，徘徊五間。

translations.literal: Descending from the precinct, each face had three gates, together forming one structure, each gate-bay having five bays.
translations.idiomatic: Below the precinct, each face had three gates forming one structure, each gate-bay spanning five bays.

sentences.zh: 按《尚書》，一期有四時，故四面各一所開門；

translations.literal: According to the Documents, one cycle has four seasons; therefore on each face one gate-opening was set;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say one cycle has four seasons, so each face had one gate-opening;

sentences.zh: 每時有三月，故每一所開三門；

translations.literal: each season has three months, so each opening had three gates;
translations.idiomatic: with three months per season, each opening received three gates;

sentences.zh: 一期十有二月，故周回總十二門。

translations.literal: one cycle has twelve months, so in all there were twelve gates around.
translations.idiomatic: and one cycle has twelve months, for twelve gates in all around the precinct.

sentences.zh: 所以面別一門，應茲四序，既一時而統三月，故於一舍而置三門。

translations.literal: Thus one gate on each face answered the four seasons; since one season governs three months, three gates were placed in one gate-structure.
translations.idiomatic: One gate per face matched the four seasons; because one season governs three months, three gates were set in each gate-structure.

sentences.zh: 又《周易》三為陽數，二為陰數，合而為五，所以每門舍五間。

translations.literal: Again, in the Book of Changes three is the yang number and two the yin number; together they make five—hence each gate-structure had five bays.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes, three is yang and two is yin—five together—so each gate-structure had five bays.

sentences.zh: 院四隅各置重樓，其四墉各依本方色。

translations.literal: At the four corners of the precinct double towers were set, and each enclosing wall followed its direction’s color.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners stood double towers, and each enclosing wall took the color of its direction.

sentences.zh: 按《淮南子》，地有四維，故四樓。

translations.literal: According to the Huainanzi, the earth has four corners; hence four towers.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says the earth has four corners—hence four towers.

sentences.zh: 又按《月令》，水、火、金、木、土五方各異色，故其牆各依本方之色。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Monthly Ordinances, the five directions—water, fire, metal, wood, and earth—each has a distinct color; therefore each wall followed its direction’s color.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances assign distinct colors to water, fire, metal, wood, and earth—so each wall followed its direction’s color.

sentences.zh: 基八面，象八方。

translations.literal: The base had eight faces, symbolizing the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: The base was octagonal, symbolizing the eight directions.

sentences.zh: 按《周禮》「黃琮禮地」。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, “the yellow jade cube sacrifices to Earth.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say, “the yellow jade cube sacrifices to Earth.”

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注：琮者，八方之玉，以象地形，故以祀地。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan’s commentary: the cube is jade of the eight directions, symbolizing earth’s form; therefore it sacrifices to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: the cube is jade of the eight directions, symbolizing earth’s form, and thus sacrifices to Earth.

sentences.zh: 則知地形八方。

translations.literal: From this one knows the terrain has eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the terrain has eight directions.

sentences.zh: 又按《漢書》，武帝立八觚壇以祀地。

translations.literal: Again, according to the History of Han, Emperor Wu established the Eight Gu altars to sacrifice to Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han says Emperor Wu built the Eight Gu altars to sacrifice to Earth.

sentences.zh: 登地之壇，形象地，故令為八方之基，以象地形。

translations.literal: Ascending the altar to Earth symbolizes earth’s form; therefore the base was made with eight faces to symbolize the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The altar to Earth symbolizes earth’s form, so the base was made octagonal to match the terrain.

sentences.zh: 基高一丈二尺，徑二百八十尺。

translations.literal: The base was one zhang two chi high and two hundred eighty chi in diameter.
translations.idiomatic: The base stood one zhang two chi high and two hundred eighty chi across.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，陽為六律，陰為六呂。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, yang is the six pitch-pipes and yin the six secondary pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han treats yang as the six pitch-pipes and yin as the six secondary pipes.

sentences.zh: 陽與陰合，故高一丈二尺。

translations.literal: Yang and yin join; therefore the height is one zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and yin join—hence the height of one zhang two chi.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，三為陽數，八為陰數。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, three is the yang number and eight the yin number.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes three yang and eight yin.

sentences.zh: 三八相乘，得二百四十尺。

translations.literal: Three and eight multiplied yield two hundred forty chi.
translations.idiomatic: Three times eight gives two hundred forty chi.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，九會之數有四十，合為二百八十，所以基徑二百八十尺。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, the nine conjunctions’ tally has forty; together they make two hundred eighty—hence the base diameter of two hundred eighty chi.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han’s tally of nine conjunctions adds forty to two hundred forty—two hundred eighty—fixing the base diameter.

sentences.zh: 故以交通天地之和，錯綜陰陽之數。

translations.literal: Thus Heaven and Earth’s harmonies were joined and yin-yang numbers interwoven.
translations.idiomatic: So Heaven and Earth’s harmonies met and yin-yang numbers were woven together.

sentences.zh: 以明陽不獨運，資陰和以助成；

translations.literal: To show yang does not move alone but borrows yin’s harmony to complete its work;
translations.idiomatic: Yang does not move alone but borrows yin’s harmony to finish its work;

sentences.zh: 陰不孤行，待陽唱而方應。

translations.literal: yin does not proceed alone but waits for yang’s lead before responding.
translations.idiomatic: yin does not act alone but waits for yang’s lead before answering.

sentences.zh: 陰陽兩順，天地咸亨，則百寶斯興，九疇攸序。

translations.literal: When yin and yang both accord and Heaven and Earth are all penetrating, the hundred treasures arise and the nine categories are ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang accord and Heaven and Earth penetrate, the hundred treasures arise and the nine categories fall into order.

sentences.zh: 基每面三階，周回十二階，每階為二十五級。

translations.literal: Each face of the base had three steps, twelve steps around, each step having twenty-five treads.
translations.idiomatic: Each face of the base had three steps—twelve around—with twenty-five treads per step.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，天有三階，故每面三階；

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, Heaven has three steps; therefore three steps on each face;
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han says Heaven has three steps—hence three steps on each face;

sentences.zh: 地有十二辰，故周回十二階。

translations.literal: Earth has the twelve chronograms; therefore twelve steps around.
translations.idiomatic: Earth has the twelve chronograms—hence twelve steps around.

sentences.zh: 又按《文子》，從凡至聖，有二十五等，故每階二十五級。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Wenzi, from the common to the sage there are twenty-five grades; therefore twenty-five treads per step.
translations.idiomatic: The Wenzi counts twenty-five grades from commoner to sage—hence twenty-five treads per step.

sentences.zh: 所以應符星而設階，法台耀以疏陛，上擬霄漢之儀，下則地辰之數。

translations.literal: Thus steps answered the asterisms and patterned the terrace’s glory in the steps, above matching the azure vault’s rites and below following the earthly chronograms’ numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Steps matched the asterisms and patterned the terrace’s glory, above echoing the azure vault and below the earthly chronograms.

sentences.zh: 又列茲重級，用准聖凡。

translations.literal: These repeated grades also measured sage against commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The graded steps also measured sage against commoner.

sentences.zh: 象皇極之高居，俯庶類而臨耀。

translations.literal: They symbolized the august pole’s high dwelling, looking down on the myriad kinds in radiance.
translations.idiomatic: They symbolized the august pole’s height, looking down on all creatures in radiance.

sentences.zh: 基之上為一堂，其宇上圓。

translations.literal: Above the base stood a single hall, its roof-space round above.
translations.idiomatic: Above the base stood one hall with a round upper roof-space.

sentences.zh: 按《道德經》：天得一以清，地得一以甯，侯王得一以為天下貞。

translations.literal: According to the Classic of the Way and Its Power: Heaven obtaining One becomes clear, Earth obtaining One becomes tranquil, and lords obtaining One become the world’s standard.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of the Way says Heaven with One grows clear, Earth with One grows still, and rulers with One become the world’s standard.

sentences.zh: 又曰：道生一，一生二，二生三，三生萬物。

translations.literal: It also says: the Way gives birth to One; One gives birth to Two; Two gives birth to Three; Three gives birth to the ten thousand things.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: the Way begets One; One begets Two; Two begets Three; Three begets the ten thousand things.

sentences.zh: 又按《漢書》：太極元氣，函三為一。

translations.literal: Again, according to the History of Han: the Grand Ultimate’s primordial qi enfolds three as one.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han says the Grand Ultimate’s primordial qi enfolds three as one.

sentences.zh: 又曰：天子以四海為家。

translations.literal: It also says: the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his house.
translations.idiomatic: It also says the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his house.

sentences.zh: 故置一堂以象元氣，並取四海為家之義。

translations.literal: Therefore one hall was set to symbolize primordial qi and also to take the meaning of the four seas as home.
translations.idiomatic: Hence one hall symbolized primordial qi and the four seas as home.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》，「蒼璧禮天」。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Rites of Zhou, “the green jade disc sacrifices to Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou say, “the green jade disc sacrifices to Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注：璧圓以象天。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan’s commentary: the disc is round to symbolize Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: the disc is round to symbolize Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故為宇上圓。

translations.literal: Therefore the roof-space was made round above.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the upper roof-space was round.

sentences.zh: 堂每面九間，各廣一丈九尺。

translations.literal: Each face of the hall had nine bays, each bay one zhang nine chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: Each face of the hall had nine bays, each one zhang nine chi wide.

sentences.zh: 按《尚書》，地有九州，故立九間。

translations.literal: According to the Documents, Earth has nine regions; therefore nine bays were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say Earth has nine regions—hence nine bays.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，陰數十，故間別一丈九尺，所以規模厚地，準則陰陽，法二氣以通基，置九州於一宇。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, ten is the yin number; therefore each bay was one zhang nine chi wide—thus patterning the thick earth, taking yin-yang as standard, joining the two qi through the base, and placing the nine regions in one hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes ten yin—hence bays of one zhang nine chi, patterning the thick earth, fixing yin-yang, joining the two qi at the base, and gathering the nine regions in one hall.

sentences.zh: 堂周回十二門，每門高一丈七尺，闊一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Twelve gates went around the hall; each gate was one zhang seven chi high and one zhang three chi wide.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve gates encircled the hall, each one zhang seven chi high and one zhang three chi wide.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記》，一歲有十二月，所以置十二門。

translations.literal: According to the Record of Rites, one year has twelve months; therefore twelve gates were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites gives twelve months in a year—hence twelve gates.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，陰數十，陽數七，故高一丈七尺；

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, ten is the yin number and seven the yang number; therefore the height is one zhang seven chi;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes ten yin and seven yang—hence height of one zhang seven chi;

sentences.zh: 又曰陽數五，陰數八，故闊一丈三尺。

translations.literal: it also says five is yang and eight yin; therefore the width is one zhang three chi.
translations.idiomatic: five yang and eight yin fix the width at one zhang three chi.

sentences.zh: 所以調茲玉燭，應彼金輝，葉二氣以迴圈，逐四序而迎節。

translations.literal: Thus the jade candle was tuned and the golden splendor answered; the two qi turned in cycle and the four seasons were welcomed in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the jade candle was tuned, golden splendor answered, the two qi cycled, and the four seasons were welcomed in turn.

sentences.zh: 堂周回二十四窗，高一丈三尺，闊一丈一尺，二十三櫺，二十四明。

translations.literal: Twenty-four windows went around the hall, each one zhang three chi high and one zhang one chi wide, with twenty-three lattice-bars and twenty-four lights.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four windows encircled the hall, each one zhang three chi high and one zhang one chi wide, with twenty-three lattice-bars and twenty-four lights.

sentences.zh: 按《史記》，天有二十四氣，故置二十四窗。

translations.literal: According to the Records of the Historian, Heaven has twenty-four qi; therefore twenty-four windows were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Records say Heaven has twenty-four qi—hence twenty-four windows.

sentences.zh: 又按《書》，一年十二月，並象閏，故高一丈三尺。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Documents, twelve months in a year, including the intercalation, symbolized in the height of one zhang three chi.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents’ twelve months plus intercalation are echoed in the height of one zhang three chi.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，天數一，地數十，故闊一丈一尺；

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, Heaven’s number is one and Earth’s ten; therefore the width is one zhang one chi;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes makes Heaven one and Earth ten—width one zhang one chi;

sentences.zh: 又天數九，地數十，並四時成二十三，故二十三櫺。

translations.literal: Heaven’s number nine and Earth’s ten, with the four seasons making twenty-three, yield twenty-three lattice-bars.
translations.idiomatic: nine and ten with the four seasons yield twenty-three lattice-bars.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，八純卦之本體，合二十四爻，故有二十四明。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, the eight pure hexagrams in their basic bodies, totaling twenty-four lines, give twenty-four lights.
translations.idiomatic: The eight pure hexagrams’ twenty-four lines give twenty-four lights.

sentences.zh: 列牖疏窗，象風候氣，遠周天地之數，曲准陰陽之和。

translations.literal: Windows ranged in rows, symbolizing wind and seasonal qi, broadly encompassing Heaven and Earth’s numbers and closely matching yin-yang’s harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked windows symbolized wind and seasonal qi, spanning Heaven and Earth’s numbers and matching yin-yang’s harmony.

sentences.zh: 堂心八柱，各長五十五尺。

translations.literal: At the hall’s center were eight pillars, each fifty-five chi long.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pillars stood at the hall’s center, each fifty-five chi tall.

sentences.zh: 按《河圖》，八柱承天，故置八柱。

translations.literal: According to the River Chart, eight pillars bear Heaven; therefore eight pillars were set.
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart says eight pillars bear Heaven—hence eight pillars.

sentences.zh: 又按《周易》，大衍之數五十有五，故長五十五尺。

translations.literal: Again, according to the Book of Changes, the Great Expansion’s number is fifty-five; therefore the length is fifty-five chi.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes’ Great Expansion number is fifty-five—hence fifty-five chi.

sentences.zh: 聳茲八柱，承彼九間，數該大衍之規，形符立極之制。

translations.literal: These eight pillars rose to bear the nine bays—number matching the Great Expansion’s rule, form matching the established pole’s design.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pillars rose to bear nine bays—number matching Great Expansion, form matching the established pole.

sentences.zh: 且柱為陰數，天實陽元，柱以陰氣上升，天以陽和下降，固陰陽之交泰，乃天地之相承。

translations.literal: Moreover pillars are yin in number while Heaven is truly yang in origin; pillars rise by yin qi while Heaven descends by yang harmony—thus yin and yang interchange and Heaven and Earth succeed each other.
translations.idiomatic: Pillars are yin in number while Heaven is yang in origin; pillars rise on yin qi as Heaven descends in yang harmony—yin and yang interchange and Heaven and Earth succeed each other.

sentences.zh: 堂心之外，置四柱為四輔。

translations.literal: Outside the hall’s center, four pillars were set as the Four Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the central eight pillars stood four more as the Four Assistants.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，天有四輔星，故置四柱以象四星。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, Heaven has four Assistant stars; therefore four pillars were set to symbolize the four stars.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han names four Assistant stars—hence four pillars symbolizing them.

sentences.zh: 內以八柱承天，外象四輔明化，上交下泰，表裏相成，葉台耀以分輝，契編珠而拱極。

translations.literal: Within, eight pillars bore Heaven; without, four Assistants displayed transformation—above communicating, below penetrating, inner and outer completing each other, matching the terrace’s glory in divided radiance and stringing pearls to embrace the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Eight pillars bore Heaven within; four Assistants displayed transformation without—above and below in communication, inner and outer complete, sharing the terrace’s glory and stringing pearls around the pole.

sentences.zh: 八柱四輔之外，第一重二十柱。

translations.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the first ring had twenty pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the eight pillars and four Assistants, the first ring held twenty pillars.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，天數五，地數十，並五行之數合而為二十，故置二十柱。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Heaven’s number five and Earth’s ten, together with the Five Phases’ number, total twenty; therefore twenty pillars were set.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s five, Earth’s ten, and the Five Phases make twenty—hence twenty pillars.

sentences.zh: 體二儀而立數，葉五位以裁規，式符立極之功，允應剛柔之道。

translations.literal: Embodying the Two Modes in number, matching the Five Positions in measure, conforming to the established pole’s achievement, and truly answering the way of firm and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: They embodied the Two Modes in number, the Five Positions in measure, the established pole’s work, and the way of firm and yielding.

sentences.zh: 八柱四輔之外，第二重二十八柱。

translations.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the second ring had twenty-eight pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, the second ring had twenty-eight pillars.

sentences.zh: 按《史記》，天有二十八宿，故有二十八柱。

translations.literal: According to the Records of the Historian, Heaven has twenty-eight lodges; therefore twenty-eight pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The Records say Heaven has twenty-eight lodges—hence twenty-eight pillars.

sentences.zh: 所以仰則乾圖，上符景宿，考編珠而紀度，觀列宿以迎時。

translations.literal: Thus looking up one matches the Qian chart, above matching the bright lodges, examining strung pearls to record degrees, and observing the lodges to welcome the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up, one matches the Qian chart and the bright lodges, strings pearls to mark degrees, and watches the lodges to welcome the seasons.

sentences.zh: 八柱四輔之外，第三重三十二柱。

translations.literal: Beyond the eight pillars and four Assistants, the third ring had thirty-two pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The third ring had thirty-two pillars.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，有八節、八政、八風、八音，四八三十二柱。
