translations.literal: According to the History of Han, there are eight nodes, eight policies, eight winds, and eight sounds—four eights make thirty-two pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han lists eight nodes, eight policies, eight winds, and eight sounds—four eights, thirty-two pillars.

sentences.zh: 調風禦節，萬物資以化成；

translations.literal: Regulating wind and governing the seasons, the ten thousand things borrow this to transform and grow;
translations.idiomatic: Regulating wind and seasons, the ten thousand things borrow this to grow;

sentences.zh: 布政流音，九區仰而貽則。

translations.literal: spreading government and flowing music, the nine regions look up and take it as model.
translations.idiomatic: spreading government and music, the nine regions look up and take it as model.

sentences.zh: 外面周回三十六柱。

translations.literal: On the outside, thirty-six pillars went all around.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, thirty-six pillars ran all around.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，一期三十六旬，故法之以置三十六柱。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, one cycle has thirty-six ten-day weeks; therefore thirty-six pillars were patterned on this.
translations.idiomatic: One cycle has thirty-six ten-day weeks—hence thirty-six outer pillars.

sentences.zh: 所以象歲時而致用，順寒暑以通微，璿璣之度無愆，玉曆之期永契。

translations.literal: Thus the seasons were symbolized for use, cold and heat followed in subtle accord, the armillary’s measure was without error, and the jade calendar’s term was ever in covenant.
translations.idiomatic: They symbolized the seasons for use, followed cold and heat in subtle accord, kept the armillary without error, and matched the jade calendar’s term.

sentences.zh: 八柱之外，修短總有三等。

translations.literal: Beyond the eight pillars, heights and lengths totaled three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the eight pillars, pillar heights fell into three grades.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，天、地、人為三才，故置柱長短三等。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Heaven, Earth, and Man are the Three Powers; therefore three grades of pillar length.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, Earth, and Man are the Three Powers—hence three grades of length.

sentences.zh: 所以擬三才以定位，高下相形；

translations.literal: Thus the Three Powers were imitated for position, high and low contrasting;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Three Powers fixed position, high and low contrasting;

sentences.zh: 體萬物以資生，長短兼運。

translations.literal: the ten thousand things were embodied for nurture, long and short both employed.
translations.idiomatic: the ten thousand things were nurtured, long and short both employed.

sentences.zh: 八柱之外，都合一百二十柱。

translations.literal: Beyond the eight pillars, the total was one hundred twenty pillars.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the eight pillars, pillars totaled one hundred twenty.

sentences.zh: 按《禮記》，天子置三公、九卿、二十七大夫、八十一元士，合為一百二十，是以置一百二十柱。

translations.literal: According to the Record of Rites, the Son of Heaven appoints three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one elemental officers—totaling one hundred twenty; therefore one hundred twenty pillars were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites counts three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one elemental officers—one hundred twenty—hence one hundred twenty pillars.

sentences.zh: 分職設官，翊化資於多士；

translations.literal: Dividing offices and setting officials, aiding transformation relies on many scholars;
translations.idiomatic: Offices divided and officials set, transformation relies on many scholars;

sentences.zh: 開物成務，構春廈藉於群材。

translations.literal: opening things and accomplishing tasks, building the spring hall borrows the host of talents.
translations.idiomatic: opening things and accomplishing tasks, the spring hall rests on a host of talents.

sentences.zh: 其上檻周回二百四柱。

translations.literal: Above them the railing-courses went around in two hundred fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Above, railing-courses ran two hundred fourteen around.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，坤之策一百四十有四，又《漢書》，九會之數有六十，故置二百四柱。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Kun’s tally is one hundred forty-four; again, the History of Han’s nine conjunctions’ tally has sixty—therefore two hundred fourteen railing-courses.
translations.idiomatic: Kun’s tally is one hundred forty-four and the History of Han’s nine conjunctions add sixty—two hundred fourteen railing-courses.

sentences.zh: 所以采坤策之玄妙，法甲乙之精微，環回契辰象之規，結構准陰陽之數。

translations.literal: Thus Kun’s tally’s subtle mystery was taken, the jia-yi cycle’s refinement was patterned, circling to match the asterisms’ rule and structuring to match yin-yang’s numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They took Kun’s subtle tally, patterned the jia-yi refinement, circled to match the asterisms, and structured to yin-yang’s numbers.

sentences.zh: 又基以象地，故葉策於坤元；

translations.literal: Again, because the base symbolizes Earth, the tally was applied to Kun’s origin;
translations.idiomatic: Because the base symbolizes Earth, the tally was applied to Kun’s origin;

sentences.zh: 柱各依方，復規模於甲子。

translations.literal: each pillar followed its direction, again patterning the jiazi cycle.
translations.idiomatic: pillars followed their directions, again mapping the sexagenary cycle.

sentences.zh: 重楣，二百一十六條。

translations.literal: Double lintels: two hundred sixteen pieces.
translations.idiomatic: There were two hundred sixteen double lintels.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，乾之策二百一十有六，故置二百一十六條。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Qian’s tally is two hundred sixteen; therefore two hundred sixteen pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s tally is two hundred sixteen—hence two hundred sixteen lintels.

sentences.zh: 所以規模《易》象，擬法乾元，應大衍之深玄，葉神策之至數。

translations.literal: Thus the Changes’ image was patterned, Qian’s origin was taken as model, the Great Expansion’s deep mystery was answered, and the divine tally’s ultimate number was matched.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Changes’ image was patterned, Qian’s origin modeled, Great Expansion answered, and the divine tally matched.

sentences.zh: 大小節級拱，總六千三百四十五。

translations.literal: Large and small bracket-arms and tiered arches totaled six thousand three hundred forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Bracket-arms large and small and tiered arches numbered six thousand three hundred forty-five.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，會月之數，六千三百四十五，故置六千三百四十五枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, the conjunction-month number is six thousand three hundred forty-five; therefore six thousand three hundred forty-five pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han’s conjunction-month number is six thousand three hundred forty-five—hence that many bracket pieces.

sentences.zh: 所以遠采三統之文，傍符會月之數，契金儀而調節，偶璿曆以和時。

translations.literal: Thus the Three Systems’ text was drawn from afar, the conjunction-month number was matched beside it, golden measures were joined in regulation, and the jade calendar was paired to harmonize the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: They drew on the Three Systems, matched the conjunction-month number, joined golden measures, and paired the jade calendar to the seasons.

sentences.zh: 重幹，四百八十九枚。

translations.literal: Double rafters: four hundred eighty-nine pieces.
translations.idiomatic: There were four hundred eighty-nine double rafters.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，章月二百三十五，閏月周回二百五十四，總成四百八十九，故置四百八十九枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, rule-months are two hundred thirty-five and intercalary months in full cycle two hundred fifty-four, totaling four hundred eighty-nine; therefore four hundred eighty-nine pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: Rule-months are two hundred thirty-five and intercalary months two hundred fifty-four—four hundred eighty-nine—hence that many double rafters.

sentences.zh: 所以法履端之奧義，象舉正之芳猷，規模曆象，發明章、閏。

translations.literal: Thus the subtle meaning of fixing the beginning was patterned, the fine plan of raising the standard was symbolized, calendrical images were patterned, and rule and intercalation were displayed.
translations.idiomatic: They patterned fixing the beginning, symbolized raising the standard, modeled calendrical images, and displayed rule and intercalation.

sentences.zh: 下璟，七十二枚。

translations.literal: Lower ring-beams: seventy-two pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two lower ring-beams were set.

sentences.zh: 按《易緯》，有七十二候，故置七十二枚。

translations.literal: According to the Apocrypha of the Changes, there are seventy-two hou; therefore seventy-two pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes apocrypha lists seventy-two hou—hence seventy-two lower ring-beams.

sentences.zh: 所以式模芳節，取規貞候，契至和於昌曆，偶神數於休期。

translations.literal: Thus fine seasons were patterned as model, true hou were taken as measure, utmost harmony was joined to the flourishing calendar, and divine numbers were paired to the auspicious term.
translations.idiomatic: They patterned fine seasons, measured true hou, joined utmost harmony to the flourishing calendar, and paired divine numbers to the auspicious term.

sentences.zh: 上璟，八十四枚。

translations.literal: Upper ring-beams: eighty-four pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty-four upper ring-beams were set.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，九會之數有七十八。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, the nine conjunctions’ number has seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Han’s nine conjunctions number seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 又按《莊子》：六合之外，聖人存而不論。

translations.literal: Again, according to Zhuangzi: “Beyond the six directions, the sage stores but does not discuss.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says, “Beyond the six directions, the sage stores but does not discuss.”

sentences.zh: 司馬彪注：天地四方為六合。

translations.literal: Sima Biao’s commentary: Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters are the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao explains: Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters are the six directions.

sentences.zh: 總成八十四，故置八十四枚。

translations.literal: Together they make eighty-four; therefore eighty-four pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: Together they make eighty-four—hence eighty-four upper ring-beams.

sentences.zh: 所以模範二儀，包羅六合，准會陰陽之數，周通氣候之源。

translations.literal: Thus the Two Modes were patterned as model, the six directions were embraced, the conjunction numbers were matched, and the sources of seasonal qi were fully joined.
translations.idiomatic: They patterned the Two Modes, embraced the six directions, matched conjunction numbers, and joined the sources of seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 枅，六十枚。

translations.literal: Tenons: sixty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty tenons were set.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，推太歲之法有六十，故置六十枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, the method for calculating the Grand Year has sixty; therefore sixty pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Year cycle has sixty steps—hence sixty tenons.

sentences.zh: 所以兼該歷數，包括陰陽，采甲乙之深微，窮辰子之玄奧。

translations.literal: Thus calendrical numbers were comprehensively covered, yin and yang were included, the jia-yi subtlety was taken, and the chen-zi mystery was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They covered calendrical numbers, embraced yin and yang, took jia-yi subtlety, and exhausted the chen-zi mystery.

sentences.zh: 連栱，三百六十枚。

translations.literal: Linked bracket-arms: three hundred sixty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred sixty linked bracket-arms were set.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，當期之日，三百有六十，故置三百六十枚。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, days in a full cycle are three hundred sixty; therefore three hundred sixty pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: A full cycle has three hundred sixty days—hence three hundred sixty linked bracket-arms.

sentences.zh: 所以葉周天之度，准當期之日，順平分而成歲，應晷運以迴圈。

translations.literal: Thus the Zhou Heaven’s measure was matched, the days of a full cycle were taken as standard, equal division completed the year, and gnomon motion turned in cycle.
translations.idiomatic: They matched the Zhou Heaven’s measure, took the full cycle’s days as standard, divided the year equally, and turned with the gnomon’s motion.

sentences.zh: 小梁，六十枚。

translations.literal: Small beams: sixty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty small beams were set.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，有六十甲子，故置六十枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, there are sixty jiazi; therefore sixty pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty jiazi—hence sixty small beams.

sentences.zh: 構此虹梁，遐規鳳曆，傍竦四宇之制，遙符六甲之源。

translations.literal: Constructing these rainbow beams, the distant Phoenix calendar was patterned; rising beside the four quarters’ design, it matched the six jia source from afar.
translations.idiomatic: These rainbow beams patterned the distant Phoenix calendar and, rising beside the four quarters’ design, matched the six jia from afar.

sentences.zh: 牽，二百二十八枚。

translations.literal: Ties: two hundred twenty-eight pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred twenty-eight ties were set.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，章中二百二十八，故置二百二十八枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, within a rule are two hundred twenty-eight; therefore two hundred twenty-eight pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: Within a rule are two hundred twenty-eight—hence that many ties.

sentences.zh: 所以應長曆之規，象中月之度，廣綜陰陽之數，傍通寒暑之和。

translations.literal: Thus the long calendar’s rule was answered, the mid-month’s measure was symbolized, yin-yang numbers were broadly interwoven, and cold-heat harmony was joined beside.
translations.idiomatic: They answered the long calendar’s rule, symbolized the mid-month’s measure, interwove yin-yang numbers, and joined cold-heat harmony.

sentences.zh: 方衡，一十五重。

translations.literal: Square cross-beams: fifteen tiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen tiers of square cross-beams were set.

sentences.zh: 按《尚書》，五行生數一十有五，故置十五重。

translations.literal: According to the Documents, the Five Phases’ birth-numbers total fifteen; therefore fifteen tiers were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases’ birth-numbers total fifteen—hence fifteen tiers.

sentences.zh: 結棟分間，法五行而演秘；

translations.literal: Binding rafters and dividing bays, the Five Phases were patterned to unfold mystery;
translations.idiomatic: Binding rafters and dividing bays, they patterned the Five Phases to unfold mystery;

sentences.zh: 疏楹疊構，葉生數以成規。

translations.literal: spacing pillars in layered structure, birth-numbers were matched to complete the rule.
translations.idiomatic: layering pillars, they matched birth-numbers to complete the rule.

sentences.zh: 南北大樑，二根。

translations.literal: Great beams north and south: two.
translations.idiomatic: Two great beams ran north and south.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》太極生兩儀，故置二大樑。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, the Grand Ultimate gives birth to the Two Modes; therefore two great beams were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ultimate begets the Two Modes—hence two great beams.

sentences.zh: 軌範乾坤，模擬天地，象玄黃之合德，表覆載以生成。

translations.literal: Patterning Qian and Kun, modeling Heaven and Earth, symbolizing the black-yellow union of virtue, displaying covering and bearing to generate.
translations.idiomatic: They patterned Qian and Kun, modeled Heaven and Earth, symbolized black-yellow union, and displayed covering and bearing.

sentences.zh: 陽馬，三十六道。

translations.literal: Sun horses: thirty-six courses.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six sun-horse courses were laid.

sentences.zh: 按《易緯》，有三十六節，故置三十六道。

translations.literal: According to the Apocrypha of the Changes, there are thirty-six nodes; therefore thirty-six courses were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes apocrypha lists thirty-six nodes—hence thirty-six sun-horse courses.

sentences.zh: 所以顯茲嘉節，契此貞辰，分六氣以燮陰陽，環四象而調風雨。

translations.literal: Thus these fine nodes were displayed, these true chronograms were joined, the six qi were divided to harmonize yin and yang, and the four images were circled to regulate wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: They displayed fine nodes, joined true chronograms, divided the six qi to harmonize yin and yang, and circled the four images to regulate wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 椽，二千九百九十根。

translations.literal: Rafters: two thousand nine hundred ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Rafters numbered two thousand nine hundred ninety.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，月法二千三百九十二，通法五百九十八，共成二千九百九十。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, the month method is two thousand three hundred ninety-two and the communication method five hundred ninety-eight, together making two thousand nine hundred ninety.
translations.idiomatic: The month method is two thousand three hundred ninety-two and the communication method five hundred ninety-eight—two thousand nine hundred ninety together.

sentences.zh: 所以偶推步之規，合通法之數。

translations.literal: Thus the step-calculation rule was paired and the communication method’s number joined.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the step-calculation rule was paired and the communication number joined.

sentences.zh: 是知疏椽構宇，則大壯之架斯隆，積月成年，則會曆之規無爽。

translations.literal: From this one knows that spacing rafters to construct the hall, the Great Strength’s frame is thereby lofty; months accumulating to a year, the conjunction calendar’s rule is without error.
translations.idiomatic: Spacing rafters to build the hall raises the Great Strength frame; months accumulating to a year keep the conjunction calendar without error.

sentences.zh: 大梠，兩重，重別三十六條，總七十二。

translations.literal: Large rafters: two tiers, each tier thirty-six pieces, seventy-two in all.
translations.idiomatic: Large rafters: two tiers of thirty-six each—seventy-two in all.

sentences.zh: 按《淮南子》，太平之時，五日一風，一年有七十二風，故置七十二條。

translations.literal: According to the Huainanzi, in the age of Great Peace a wind came every five days and in one year there were seventy-two winds; therefore seventy-two pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says Great Peace brought a wind every five days—seventy-two winds a year—hence seventy-two large rafters.

sentences.zh: 所以通規瑞曆，葉數祥風，遙符淳俗之年，遠則休征之契。

translations.literal: Thus the auspicious calendar’s rule was joined, auspicious winds were matched in number, the pure age’s year was matched from afar, and the restful omen’s covenant was followed distantly.
translations.idiomatic: They joined the auspicious calendar, matched auspicious winds in number, echoed the pure age’s year, and followed the restful omen’s covenant.

sentences.zh: 飛簷椽，七百二十九枚。

translations.literal: Flying-eave rafters: seven hundred twenty-nine pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty-nine flying-eave rafters were set.

sentences.zh: 按《漢書》，從子至午，其數七百二十九，故置七百二十九枚。

translations.literal: According to the History of Han, from the zi hour to the wu hour the number is seven hundred twenty-nine; therefore seven hundred twenty-nine pieces were set.
translations.idiomatic: From zi to wu the number is seven hundred twenty-nine—hence that many flying-eave rafters.

sentences.zh: 所以采辰象之宏模，法周天之至數。

translations.literal: Thus the asterisms’ grand pattern was taken and the Zhou Heaven’s ultimate number was patterned.
translations.idiomatic: They took the asterisms’ grand pattern and patterned the Zhou Heaven’s ultimate number.

sentences.zh: 且午為陰本，子實陽源，子午分時，則生成之道自著；

translations.literal: Moreover wu is yin’s root and zi is truly yang’s source; zi and wu divide the hours and the way of generation is thereby displayed;
translations.idiomatic: Wu is yin’s root and zi yang’s source; dividing the hours at zi and wu shows the way of generation;

sentences.zh: 陰陽合德，則覆載之義茲隆。

translations.literal: when yin and yang unite in virtue, the meaning of covering and bearing is thereby exalted.
translations.idiomatic: when yin and yang unite in virtue, covering and bearing are exalted.

sentences.zh: 堂簷，徑二百八十八尺。

translations.literal: The hall eaves’ diameter: two hundred eighty-eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: The hall eaves spanned two hundred eighty-eight chi in diameter.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，乾之策二百一十六，《易緯》雲，年有七十二候，合為二百八十八，故徑二百八十八尺。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Qian’s tally is two hundred sixteen; the Apocrypha of the Changes says the year has seventy-two hou—together two hundred eighty-eight; therefore the diameter is two hundred eighty-eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s tally is two hundred sixteen and the Changes apocrypha adds seventy-two hou—two hundred eighty-eight—fixing the eaves’ diameter.

sentences.zh: 所以仰葉乾策，遠承貞候，順和氣而調序，擬圓蓋以照臨。

translations.literal: Thus Qian’s tally was matched above, true hou were joined from afar, harmonious qi was followed in sequence, and the round canopy was imitated for oversight.
translations.idiomatic: They matched Qian’s tally above, joined true hou from afar, followed harmonious qi in sequence, and imitated the round canopy for oversight.

sentences.zh: 堂上棟，去基上面九十尺。

translations.literal: The hall’s upper ridge-beam was ninety chi above the base’s top surface.
translations.idiomatic: The upper ridge-beam stood ninety chi above the base’s top.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，天數九，地數十，以九乘十，數當九十，故去基上面九十尺。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, Heaven’s number is nine and Earth’s ten; nine times ten yields ninety—therefore ninety chi above the base’s top.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven nine and Earth ten—nine times ten is ninety—hence ninety chi above the base.

sentences.zh: 所以上法圓清，下儀方載，契陰陽之至數，葉交泰之貞符。

translations.literal: Thus above patterned round clarity and below imitated square bearing, matching yin-yang’s ultimate numbers and joining the covenant of interchange.
translations.idiomatic: Above patterned round clarity, below square bearing, matching yin-yang’s ultimate numbers and interchange’s covenant.

sentences.zh: 又以茲天九，乘於地十，象陽唱而陰和，法乾施而坤成。

translations.literal: Again, taking Heaven’s nine and multiplying by Earth’s ten symbolizes yang’s lead and yin’s response, patterning Qian’s bestowal and Kun’s completion.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven’s nine times Earth’s ten symbolizes yang leading and yin answering, Qian bestowing and Kun completing.

sentences.zh: 簷，去地五十五尺。

translations.literal: The eaves were fifty-five chi above the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The eaves stood fifty-five chi above the ground.

sentences.zh: 按《周易》，大衍之數五十有五，故去地五十五尺。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Changes, the Great Expansion’s number is fifty-five; therefore fifty-five chi above the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Expansion number is fifty-five—hence eaves fifty-five chi high.

sentences.zh: 所以擬大《易》之嘉數，通惟神之至賾，道合萬象，理貫三才。

translations.literal: Thus the great Changes’ fine number was imitated, the utmost spirit’s deep mystery was joined—principle embracing the ten thousand images, pattern threading the Three Powers.
translations.idiomatic: They imitated the great Changes’ number, joined the utmost spirit’s mystery—principle embracing all images, pattern threading the Three Powers.

sentences.zh: 上以清陽玉葉覆之。

translations.literal: Above, clear yang was covered with jade leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Above, clear yang was roofed with jade leaves.

sentences.zh: 按《淮南子》，清陽為天，合以清陽之色。

translations.literal: According to the Huainanzi, clear yang is Heaven; it was joined with clear yang’s color.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi makes clear yang Heaven—hence roofing in clear yang’s color.

sentences.zh: 詔下之後，猶群議未決。

translations.literal: After the edict was issued, the various factions still had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: After the edict, factions still had not settled the matter.

sentences.zh: 終高宗之世，未能創立。

translations.literal: Through Gaozong’s reign it was never established.
translations.idiomatic: Through Emperor Gaozong’s reign it was never built.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，儒者屢上言請創明堂。

translations.literal: When Empress Zetian held court, Confucians repeatedly memorialized asking to build the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held court, scholars repeatedly asked to build the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 則天以高宗遺意，乃與北門學士議其制，不聽群言。

translations.literal: Zetian, following Gaozong’s last intent, then discussed its design with Northern Gate academicians and would not heed the multitude’s opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Following Gaozong’s last intent, Wu discussed the design with Northern Gate academicians and would not heed wider opinion.

sentences.zh: 垂拱三年春，毀東都之乾元殿，就其地創之。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Chuigong, the Qianyuan Hall of the eastern capital was demolished and the Bright Hall was built on its site.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Chuigong year 3, Luoyang’s Qianyuan Hall was torn down and the Bright Hall built on its site.

sentences.zh: 四年正月五日，明堂成。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the fourth year, the Bright Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the first month, year 4, the Bright Hall was completed.

sentences.zh: 凡高二百九十四尺，東西南北各三百尺。

translations.literal: In all it was two hundred ninety-four chi high; east, west, south, and north each three hundred chi.
translations.idiomatic: It stood two hundred ninety-four chi high; three hundred chi on each side.

sentences.zh: 有三層：下層象四時，各隨方色；

translations.literal: It had three tiers: the lower tier symbolized the four seasons, each following its direction’s color;
translations.idiomatic: It had three tiers: the lower symbolized the four seasons, each in its direction’s color;

sentences.zh: 中層法十二辰，圓蓋，蓋上盤九龍捧之；

translations.literal: the middle tier followed the twelve chronograms, with a round canopy; on the canopy a dish of nine dragons held it up;
translations.idiomatic: the middle followed the twelve chronograms under a round canopy borne on nine dragons;

sentences.zh: 上層法二十四氣，亦圓蓋。

translations.literal: the upper tier followed the twenty-four qi, also with a round canopy.
translations.idiomatic: the upper followed the twenty-four qi, also under a round canopy.

sentences.zh: 亭中有巨木十圍，上下通貫，栭、櫨ＬＲ、勣，藉以為本，亙之以鐵索。

translations.literal: In the pavilion was a great timber ten arm-spans around, running through top to bottom; bracket-arms, corbels, and bearing-blocks were borrowed as the foundation and spanned with iron cables.
translations.idiomatic: A timber ten arm-spans thick ran through the pavilion; bracket-arms, corbels, and bearing-blocks formed the core and iron cables spanned it.

sentences.zh: 蓋為鸞鷟，黃金飾之，勢若飛翥。

translations.literal: The canopy was made a phoenix-pheasant, gilded, its posture as if soaring.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy was shaped as a phoenix-pheasant, gilded, poised as if soaring.

sentences.zh: 刻木為瓦，夾紵漆之。

translations.literal: Wood was carved as tiles and lacquered between ramie layers.
translations.idiomatic: Wood was carved into tiles and lacquered between ramie layers.

sentences.zh: 明堂之下施鐵渠，以為辟雍之象。

translations.literal: Below the Bright Hall an iron channel was laid as the image of the Bright Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Bright Hall ran an iron channel symbolizing the Bright Enclosure moat.

sentences.zh: 號萬象神宮。

translations.literal: It was titled the Palace of Myriad Images.
translations.idiomatic: It was named the Palace of Myriad Images.

sentences.zh: 因改河南縣為合宮縣。

translations.literal: Henan county was therefore renamed Hegong county.
translations.idiomatic: Henan county was renamed Hegong county.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 黃軒禦曆，朝萬方于合宮；

translations.literal: The Yellow Thearch governed the calendar and received the ten thousand regions at the Hegong;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Thearch governed the calendar and received the realm at the Hegong;

sentences.zh: 丹陵握符，咨四岳於衢室。

translations.literal: Emperor Danling grasped the talisman and consulted the four peaks at the Crossroads Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Danling held the talisman and took counsel from the four peaks at the Crossroads Chamber.

sentences.zh: 有虞輯瑞，總章之號既存；

translations.literal: Emperor Shun gathered auspicious signs—the title Total Pattern already existed;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun gathered auspicious signs—the name Total Pattern already stood;

sentences.zh: 大禹錫珪，重屋之名攸建。

translations.literal: Yu the Great was granted the jade tablet—the name Layered Houses was thereupon established.
translations.idiomatic: Yu received the jade tablet—and the name Layered Houses was established.

sentences.zh: 殷人受命，置陽館以辨方；

translations.literal: The Yin received the mandate and set the Yang Lodge to distinguish directions;
translations.idiomatic: The Yin took the mandate and built the Yang Lodge to mark the directions;

sentences.zh: 周室凝圖，立明堂以經野。

translations.literal: the Zhou fixed the chart and established the Bright Hall to order the realm.
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou fixed the chart and built the Bright Hall to order the realm.

sentences.zh: 用能範圍三極，幽贊五神，展尊祖之懷，申宗祀之典。

translations.literal: Thus they could compass the Three Ultimates, assist the Five Spirits in the hidden, display reverence for ancestors, and extend the ancestral sacrifice’s canon.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they compassed the Three Ultimates, assisted the Five Spirits in secret, displayed reverence for ancestors, and extended ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 爰從漢、魏，迨及周、隋、經始之制雖興，修廣之規未備。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei down through Zhou and Sui, beginning designs arose but the rules for expansion were not complete.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei through Zhou and Sui, beginnings were made but full rules for expansion were never settled.

sentences.zh: 朕以庸昧，虔膺厚托，受寄於綴衣之夕，荷顧於仍幾之前。

translations.literal: I, in my mediocrity, reverently received the heavy trust, entrusted on the night of the mourning garment, burdened with care before the almost-fallen throne.
translations.idiomatic: I, mediocre, reverently received heavy trust, entrusted on the night of mourning, burdened before the almost-fallen throne.

sentences.zh: 伏以高宗往年，已屬意于陽館，故京輔之縣，預紀明堂之名；

translations.literal: I reflect that in former years Gaozong already set his mind on the Yang Lodge; therefore in the capital region’s counties the name Bright Hall was recorded in advance;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong had already turned his mind to the Yang Lodge; the capital counties were pre-named for the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 改元之期，先著總章之號。

translations.literal: at the change of reign title the name Total Pattern was first applied.
translations.idiomatic: and at the change of reign the name Total Pattern was applied first.

sentences.zh: 朕于乾封之際，已奉表上塵，雖簡宸心，未遑榮構。

translations.literal: At the time of Qianfeng I already submitted a memorial rising to dust; though it pleased the imperial heart, there was no leisure to honor it with construction.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianfeng I had already memorialized; though it pleased the throne, there was no leisure to build.

sentences.zh: 今以鼎郊勝壤，圭邑奧區，處天地之中，順陰陽之序，舟車是湊，貢賦攸均，爰藉子來之功，式遵奉先之旨。

translations.literal: Now at this victorious suburban site, this sacred capital’s inner region, standing in Heaven and Earth’s center and following yin-yang’s order—boats and carts converge, tribute is evenly distributed—I borrow the people’s willing labor and follow the mandate to honor the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Now at this sacred site in the capital’s center, where yin-yang order, transport, and tribute converge, I borrow willing labor and follow the mandate to honor the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 夫明堂者，天子宗祀之堂，朝諸侯之位也。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is the Son of Heaven’s hall for ancestral sacrifice and the place for receiving feudal lords in audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is where the Son of Heaven sacrifices to ancestors and receives feudal lords in audience.

sentences.zh: 開乾坤之奧策，法氣象之運行，故能使災害不生，禍亂不作。

translations.literal: It opens the hidden strategies of Qian and Kun and patterns the movement of emblems and qi—thus calamities do not arise and turmoil is not made.
translations.idiomatic: It opens Qian and Kun’s hidden strategies and patterns emblems and qi—so calamity does not arise and turmoil is not made.

sentences.zh: 眷言盛烈，豈不美歟！

translations.literal: Looking on such splendor—how is it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Such splendor—how beautiful!

sentences.zh: 比者鴻儒禮官，所執各異，鹹以為明堂者，置之三里之外，七里之內，在國陽明之地。

translations.literal: Recently the great ru and ritual officers each held a different view; all thought the Bright Hall should be placed three li outside and within seven li, in the state’s yang-bright ground.
translations.idiomatic: Recently ritual scholars disagreed: all said the Bright Hall should stand three li outside and within seven li, on the state’s yang-bright ground.

sentences.zh: 今既俯邇宮掖，恐黷靈祇，誠乃布政之居，未為宗祀之所。

translations.literal: Now that it is placed close below the palace quarters, I fear it profanes the spirits; it is truly a seat for spreading government, not yet a place for ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Placed so close to the palace, I fear it profanes the spirits; it is truly a seat for government, not yet a place for ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 朕乃為丙巳之地，去宮室遙遠，每月所居，因時饗祭，常備文物，動有煩勞，在於朕懷，殊非所謂。

translations.literal: I am in the bingsi quarter, far from the palace halls; each month I move residence for seasonal offerings, constantly keeping ritual vessels in readiness—a constant burden, and in my heart this is hardly what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: My seat lies in the bingsi quarter, far from the palace halls; each month I shift residence for seasonal rites, keeping vessels always in readiness—a constant burden, and hardly what I intend.

sentences.zh: 今故裁基紫掖，辟宇彤闈，經始肇興，成之匪日。

translations.literal: Now therefore we trim the foundation at the Purple Forbidden, open chambers at the red gate; the work has just begun and will not take many days to finish.
translations.idiomatic: We have trimmed the foundation at the Purple Forbidden and opened chambers at the red gate; the work has only begun, yet it will not take many days to finish.

sentences.zh: 但敬事天地，神明之德乃彰；

translations.literal: Only when one reverently serves Heaven and Earth does the virtue of the spirits and gods shine forth;
translations.idiomatic: Only when Heaven and Earth are served with reverence does the virtue of spirits and gods shine forth;

sentences.zh: 尊祀祖宗，嚴恭之志方展。

translations.literal: only when one honors and sacrifices to the ancestors does the will of solemn respect unfold.
translations.idiomatic: only when ancestors are honored in sacrifice does solemn respect unfold.

sentences.zh: 若使惟云布政，負扆臨人，則茅宇土階，取適而已，豈必勞百姓之力，制九筵而禦哉！

translations.literal: If one speaks only of dispensing government while leaning on the screen to face the people, then a thatched roof and earthen steps would suffice—why must one weary the people's strength and build nine mats to receive them!
translations.idiomatic: If governance alone were the aim—leaning on the screen to face the realm—a thatched roof and earthen steps would suffice. Why weary the people and build nine mats to receive them?

sentences.zh: 誠以獲執蘋蘩，虔奉宗廟故也。

translations.literal: Truly it is because one obtains and holds the water-plant offerings and reverently serves the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Truly it is to hold the offerings and serve the ancestral temple with reverence.

sentences.zh: 時既沿革，莫或相遵，自我作古，用適於事。

translations.literal: Times have changed and none follow the old; I myself make the antiquity, fitting it to the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Times have changed and none follow the old; we make the rite anew, fitting it to present need.

sentences.zh: 今以上堂為嚴配之所，下堂為布政之居，光敷禮訓，式展誠敬。

translations.literal: Now the upper hall is the place of solemn matching sacrifice, the lower hall the seat of dispensing government—radiating ritual instruction, displaying sincerity and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The upper hall is for solemn matching sacrifice, the lower for government—radiating ritual teaching, displaying sincerity and reverence.

sentences.zh: 來年正月一日，可于明堂宗祀三聖，以配上帝。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the coming year, one may at the Bright Hall perform the ancestral sacrifice to the Three Sages, matching them to the High God.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month next year, at the Bright Hall perform the ancestral sacrifice to the Three Sages, matching them to the High God.

sentences.zh: 宜令禮官、博士、學士、內外明禮者，詳定儀禮，務從典要，速以奏聞。

translations.literal: Let ritual officers, erudites, academicians, and all within and without who understand ritual fix the ceremonies in detail, striving for canonical essentials, and report swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Let ritual officers, erudites, academicians, and all who understand ritual within and without fix the ceremonies in detail, strive for canonical essentials, and report swiftly.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年正月元日，始親享明堂，大赦改元。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of Yongchang year 1, he first personally performed the Bright Hall sacrifice, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of Yongchang year 1, she first personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall, proclaimed a great amnesty, and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 其月四日，禦明堂布政，頒九條以訓於百官。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of that month, he attended the Bright Hall to dispense government and issued nine articles of instruction to admonish the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of that month, she attended the Bright Hall to dispense government and issued nine articles of instruction to admonish the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is lengthy and not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The text is lengthy and is not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又禦明堂，饗群臣，賜縑纁有差。

translations.literal: The next day, he again attended the Bright Hall, feasted the host of ministers, and bestowed silk and hemp cloth in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, she again attended the Bright Hall, feasted the ministers, and bestowed silk and hemp in graded amounts.

sentences.zh: 自明堂成後，縱東都婦人及諸州父老入觀，兼賜酒食，久之乃止。

translations.literal: After the Bright Hall was completed, women of the eastern capital and elders from the various prefectures were allowed to enter and view it; food and drink were also bestowed—this continued for a long time before it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After the Bright Hall was completed, women of the eastern capital and elders from the prefectures were admitted to view it; food and drink were bestowed as well—this continued long before it ceased.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃及諸夷以明堂成，亦各遣使來賀。

translations.literal: Tibet and the various Yi peoples, because the Bright Hall was completed, each also sent envoys to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet and the various Yi peoples, learning the Bright Hall was completed, each sent envoys to congratulate.

sentences.zh: 載初元年冬正月庚辰朔，日南至，復親饗明堂，大赦改元，用周正。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of winter in Zaichu year 1, gengchen, the new moon—the winter solstice—he again personally feasted at the Bright Hall, proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the era name, and adopted the Zhou calendar beginning.
translations.idiomatic: On the winter solstice, first day of the first month of Zaichu year 1, gengchen, she again personally feasted at the Bright Hall, proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the era name, and adopted the Zhou calendar.

sentences.zh: 翼日，布政於群後。

translations.literal: The next day, he dispensed government to the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, she dispensed government to the nobles.

sentences.zh: 其年二月，則天又禦明堂，大開三教。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year, Wu Zetian again attended the Bright Hall and broadly opened the Three Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year, Wu Zetian again attended the Bright Hall and broadly opened the Three Teachings

sentences.zh: 內史邢文偉講《孝經》，命侍臣及僧、道士等以次論議，日昃乃罷。

translations.literal: Inner Secretariat Director Xing Wenwei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; she ordered attending ministers and monks and Daoist masters and others to debate in turn—the sun slanted westward before they finished.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Secretariat Director Xing Wenwei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; she ordered attending ministers, monks, and Daoist masters to debate in turn until the sun stood in the west.

sentences.zh: 天授二年正月乙酉，日南至，親祀明堂，合祭天地，以周文王及武氏先考、先妣配，百神從祀，並於壇位次第布席以祀之。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the winter solstice, in the first month of Tianshou year 2, he personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall, jointly sacrificing Heaven and Earth, matching King Wen of Zhou and Wu's deceased father and mother, with the hundred spirits following in sacrifice—all at the altar seats, mats laid in sequence for worship.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the winter solstice, in the first month of Tianshou year 2, she personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall, jointly sacrificing Heaven and Earth, matching King Wen of Zhou and the Wu clan's deceased father and mother, with the hundred spirits following—all at the altar seats, mats laid in sequence.

sentences.zh: 於是春官郎中韋叔夏奏曰：「謹按明堂大享，唯祀五帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon Spring Office Gentleman Wei Shuxia memorialized: "Per your servant's examination, the Bright Hall great offering sacrifices only to the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Spring Office Gentleman Wei Shuxia memorialized: "By your servant's examination, the Bright Hall great offering sacrifices only to the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 故《月令》云：'是月也，大享帝。

translations.literal: Thus the Monthly Ordinances says: "In this month, the great offering to the Emperors."
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances says: "In this month, the great offering to the Emperors."

sentences.zh: '則《曲禮》所雲'大享不問卜'，鄭玄注雲'謂遍祭五帝於明堂，莫適卜'是也。

translations.literal: " Then what the Ceremonies says—"the great offering does not ask the tortoise"—Zheng Xuan's note explains: "meaning to sacrifice to the Five Emperors throughout at the Bright Hall, with no need to divine"—is correct.
translations.idiomatic: " What the Ceremonies calls "the great offering does not ask the tortoise"—Zheng Xuan explains as sacrificing to the Five Emperors throughout at the Bright Hall without divination—is correct.

sentences.zh: 又按《祭法》云：'祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Again per the Sacrificial Canon: "Take King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong."
translations.idiomatic: Per the Sacrificial Canon: "Take King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong."

sentences.zh: '鄭玄注云：'祭五帝、五神於明堂曰祖、宗。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's note says: "Sacrificing to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits at the Bright Hall is called zu and zong."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan notes: "Sacrificing to the Five Emperors and Five Spirits at the Bright Hall is called zu and zong."

sentences.zh: '故《孝經》云：「宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝。

translations.literal: Thus the Classic of Filial Piety says: "The zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall, matching the High God."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "The zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall, matching the High God."

sentences.zh: '據此諸文，明堂正禮，唯祀五帝，配以祖宗及五帝、五官神等，自外餘神，並不合預。

translations.literal: By these texts, the correct rite of the Bright Hall sacrifices only to the Five Emperors, matching ancestors and the Five Emperors and Five Official Spirits and the like; all other spirits beyond these should not participate.
translations.idiomatic: By these texts, the correct Bright Hall rite sacrifices only to the Five Emperors, matching ancestors and the Five Emperors and Five Official Spirits; all other spirits should not participate.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下追遠情深，崇禋志切，於明堂祀，加昊天上帝、皇地祇，重之以先帝、先後配享，此乃補前王之闕典，弘嚴配之虔誠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in pursuing the distant past, affection runs deep; in honoring the suburban sacrifice, will is keen—at the Bright Hall sacrifice adding August Heaven High God and August Earth Spirit, further matching the Former Emperor and Former Empress in joint offering: this repairs the former kings' missing canon and extends the sincerity of solemn matching sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, pursuing the distant past, affection runs deep; in honoring the suburban sacrifice, will is keen—at the Bright Hall adding August Heaven High God and August Earth Spirit, further matching the Former Emperor and Former Empress: this repairs the former kings' missing canon and extends solemn matching sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 往以神都郊壇未建，乃於明堂之下，廣祭眾神，蓋義出權時，非不刊之禮也。

translations.literal: Formerly, because the Divine Capital suburban altars were not yet built, one broadly sacrificed the host of spirits below the Bright Hall—meaning born of expedient times, not an unalterable rite.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, because the Divine Capital suburban altars were not built, the host of spirits was sacrificed below the Bright Hall—born of expedient times, not an unalterable rite.

sentences.zh: 謹按禮經：其內官、中官、五嶽、四瀆諸神，併合從祀於二至。

translations.literal: Per the ritual classics, the inner-office spirits, palace spirits, Five Marchmounts, and Four Watercourses should all follow in sacrifice at the two solstices.
translations.idiomatic: Per the ritual classics, inner-office spirits, palace spirits, the Five Marchmounts, and Four Watercourses should all follow in sacrifice at the two solstices.

sentences.zh: 明堂總奠，事乃不經。

translations.literal: A general offering at the Bright Hall is an uncanonical affair.
translations.idiomatic: A general offering at the Bright Hall is uncanonical.

sentences.zh: 然則宗祀配天之親，雜與小神同薦，于嚴敬之道，理有不安。

translations.literal: Yet the zong sacrifice matching Heaven is intimate, while miscellaneous small spirits are offered together—in the way of solemn reverence, reason finds this unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the zong sacrifice matching Heaven is intimate, while small spirits are offered together—in solemn reverence, reason finds this unsettled.

sentences.zh: 望請每歲元日，惟祀天地大神，配以帝后。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes that each year on New Year's Day only the great spirits of Heaven and Earth be sacrificed to, matching the Emperor and Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hopes that each New Year's Day only the great spirits of Heaven and Earth be sacrificed to, matching the Emperor and Empress.

sentences.zh: 其五嶽以下，請依禮于冬、夏二至，從祀方丘、圓丘，庶不煩黷。

translations.literal: For the Five Marchmounts and below, let them follow ritual at the winter and summer solstices, following sacrifice at the square mound and round mound, so that there be no troublesome repetition.
translations.idiomatic: For the Five Marchmounts and below, let them follow ritual at winter and summer solstice sacrifice at the square mound and round mound, avoiding troublesome repetition.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was accepted

sentences.zh: 時則天又於明堂後造天堂，以安佛像，高百餘尺。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Zetian also built the Hall of Paradise behind the Bright Hall to house Buddha images, more than a hundred chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Zetian also built the Hall of Paradise behind the Bright Hall to house Buddha images, more than a hundred chi high.

sentences.zh: 始起建構，為大風振倒。

translations.literal: When construction first began, a great wind shook it down.
translations.idiomatic: When construction first began, a great wind shook it down

sentences.zh: 俄又重營，其功未畢。

translations.literal: Shortly they rebuilt it, but the work was not finished.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly they rebuilt, but the work was not finished.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年正月丙申夜，佛堂災，延燒明堂，至曙，二堂並盡。

translations.literal: On the night of bingchen in the first month of Zhengsheng year 1, the Buddha hall caught fire and the blaze spread to the Bright Hall; by dawn both halls were entirely consumed.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingchen in the first month of Zhengsheng year 1, the Buddha hall caught fire and spread to the Bright Hall; by dawn both halls were entirely consumed.

sentences.zh: 尋時又無雲而雷，起自西北。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward thunder sounded though there were no clouds, rising from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward thunder sounded though there were no clouds, rising from the northwest

sentences.zh: 則天欲責躬避正殿。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian wished to blame herself and avoid the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian wished to blame herself and avoid the main hall

sentences.zh: 宰相姚璹曰：「此實人火，非是天災。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yao Shuang said: "This is truly human fire, not a heaven-sent calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yao Shuang said: "This is truly human fire, not a heaven-sent calamity

sentences.zh: 至如成周宣榭，卜代逾長；

translations.literal: As for the Zhou of King Xuan's terrace, divination showed the dynasty would long endure;
translations.idiomatic: As for King Xuan of Zhou's terrace, divination showed the dynasty would long endure;

sentences.zh: 漢武建章，盛德彌永。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace—its flourishing virtue endured ever longer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han's Jianzhang Palace—its flourishing virtue endured the longer.

sentences.zh: 今明堂是布政之所，非宗祀也。

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall is the place for dispensing government, not for ancestral sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Bright Hall is the place for dispensing government, not ancestral sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」則天乃禦端門觀酺宴，下詔令文武九品已上各上封事，極言無有所隱。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian thereupon attended the Vermilion Gate to view the communal feast, and issued an edict ordering civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above each to submit sealed memorials, speaking fully without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian thereupon attended the Vermilion Gate to view the communal feast and issued an edict ordering civil and military officials of the ninth rank and above to submit sealed memorials, speaking fully without concealment.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺劉承慶上疏曰：

translations.literal: Left Reminder Liu Chengqing submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Liu Chengqing submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞自古帝王，皆有美惡，休祥所以昭其德，災變所以知其咎，天道之常理，王者之常事。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that since antiquity emperors and kings have all had good and ill; auspicious omens thereby display their virtue, calamities and transformations thereby reveal their faults—the constant principle of Heaven's Way, the constant affair of kings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that since antiquity emperors and kings have all had good and ill; auspicious omens display their virtue, calamities reveal their faults—the constant principle of Heaven's Way, the constant affair of kings.

sentences.zh: 然則休祥屢臻，不可矜功而自滿；

translations.literal: Yet when auspicious omens arrive repeatedly, one must not boast of achievement and grow self-satisfied;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when auspicious omens arrive repeatedly, one must not boast and grow self-satisfied;

sentences.zh: 災變奄降，不可輕忽而靡驚。

translations.literal: when calamities and transformations descend suddenly, one must not treat them lightly and fail to be alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: when calamities descend suddenly, one must not treat them lightly and fail to be alarmed.

sentences.zh: 故殷宗以桑穀生朝，懷懼而自省，妖不勝德，遂立中興之功；

translations.literal: Thus the Yin ruler, when mulberry and grain grew in the court, harbored fear and examined himself—evil could not overcome virtue, and he thereupon established the achievement of restoration;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Yin ruler, when mulberry and grain grew in the court, harbored fear and examined himself—evil could not overcome virtue, and he established the achievement of restoration;

sentences.zh: 辛紂以雀生大鳥，恃福而自盈，祥不勝驕，終至傾亡之禍。

translations.literal: Xin Zhou, when a sparrow hatched a great bird, relied on fortune and grew full—auspice could not overcome arrogance, and in the end he met the calamity of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Xin, when a sparrow hatched a great bird, relied on fortune and grew full—auspice could not overcome arrogance, and in the end he met ruin.

sentences.zh: 故知災變之生，將以覺悟明主，扶持大業，使盛而不衰。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the birth of calamities and transformations is to awaken and enlighten the enlightened ruler, to support the great enterprise, so that flourishing does not decay.
translations.idiomatic: Thus calamities are born to awaken the enlightened ruler, support the great enterprise, and keep flourishing from decay.

sentences.zh: 理須祗畏神心，驚懼天誡，飭身正事，業業兢兢，則凶往而吉來，轉禍而為福。

translations.literal: Reason demands reverent fear of the spirit heart, alarm at Heaven's admonition, correcting the person and rectifying affairs, diligent and cautious—then the inauspicious departs and the auspicious comes, misfortune turns to fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Reason demands reverent fear of the spirits, alarm at Heaven's admonition, correcting the person and rectifying affairs, diligent and cautious—then the inauspicious departs, the auspicious comes, and misfortune turns to fortune.

sentences.zh: 昔殷湯禱身而降雨，成王省事以反風，宋公憂熒惑之災，而應三舍之壽，高宗懲雊鼎之異，而享百年之福，此其類也。

translations.literal: Formerly Yin Tang prayed with his person and rain fell; King Cheng reduced affairs and the wind returned; Duke Mu of Song feared the Mars calamity and received the blessing of three lodges' longevity; Emperor Gaozong chastised the crowing tripod anomaly and enjoyed a hundred years' fortune—these are of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tang prayed with his person and rain fell; King Cheng reduced affairs and the wind returned; Duke Mu of Song feared the Mars calamity and received three lodges' longevity; Emperor Gaozong chastised the crowing tripod and enjoyed a hundred years' fortune—these are of that kind.

sentences.zh: 自陛下承天理物，至道事神，美瑞嘉祥，洊臻狎委，非臣所能盡述。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty received Heaven's principle and ordered the myriad things, utmost Way serving the spirits—beautiful omens and auspicious signs arriving in succession, close and abundant—not what your servant can fully narrate.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty received Heaven's principle and ordered the myriad things, serving the spirits with utmost Way—beautiful omens arriving in succession, close and abundant—more than your servant can fully narrate.

sentences.zh: 日者變生人火，損及神宮，驚惕聖心，震動黎庶。

translations.literal: Recently human fire arose, damaging the spirit palace—alarming the sage heart, shaking the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: Recently human fire arose, damaging the spirit palace—alarming the sage heart, shaking the people.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《左傳》曰：「人火曰火，天火日災。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully per the Zuo Commentary: "Human fire is called huo; heaven fire is called zai."
translations.idiomatic: respectfully per the Zuo Commentary: "Human fire is called huo; heaven fire is called zai."

sentences.zh: 」人火因人而興，故指火體而為稱；

translations.literal: Human fire arises because of men, hence it names the fire itself;
translations.idiomatic: Human fire arises through men, hence it names the fire itself;

sentences.zh: 天火不知何起，直以所災言之。

translations.literal: heaven fire—one does not know whence it starts, and speaks only of what was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: heaven fire—one does not know whence it starts, and speaks only of what was harmed

sentences.zh: 其名雖殊，為害不別。

translations.literal: The names differ, but the harm does not.
translations.idiomatic: The names differ, but the harm does not

sentences.zh: 又《漢書·五行志》曰：「火失性則自上而降，及濫焰妄起，災宗廟，燒宮館。

translations.literal: Again the Han Documents, Treatise on the Five Phases: "When fire loses its nature it descends from above; when flames spread wantonly, it calamities the ancestral temple and burns palaces and lodges."
translations.idiomatic: Again the Han Documents, Treatise on the Five Phases: "When fire loses its nature it descends from above; when flames spread wantonly, it calamities the ancestral temple and burns palaces."

sentences.zh: 」自上而降，所謂天火；

translations.literal: Descending from above is what is called heaven fire;
translations.idiomatic: Fire descending from above is called heaven fire;

sentences.zh: 濫焰妄起，所謂人火。

translations.literal: flames spreading wantonly is what is called human fire.
translations.idiomatic: flames spreading wantonly is what is called human fire

sentences.zh: 其來雖異，為患實同。

translations.literal: Their coming differs, but the affliction is truly the same.
translations.idiomatic: Their coming differs, but the affliction is the same.

sentences.zh: 王者舉措營為，必關幽顯。

translations.literal: The king's raising, moving, building, and acting must touch the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: The king's raising, moving, building, and acting must touch the hidden and manifest

sentences.zh: 幽為天道，顯為人事，幽顯跡通，天人理合。

translations.literal: The hidden is Heaven's Way, the manifest human affairs; hidden and manifest traces connect, Heaven and human principle unite.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden is Heaven's Way, the manifest human affairs; hidden and manifest connect, Heaven and human principle unite.

sentences.zh: 今工匠宿藏其火，本無放燎之心：明堂教化之宮，復非延火之所。

translations.literal: Now craftsmen had long kept their fire—they had no mind to set a blaze: the Bright Hall is the palace of teaching and transformation, and again is not a place where fire spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Now craftsmen had long kept their fire—they had no mind to set a blaze: the Bright Hall is the palace of teaching, and again is not a place where fire spreads.

sentences.zh: 孽煨潛扇，倏忽成災，雖則因人，亦關神理。

translations.literal: Baleful flames were secretly fanned and in a moment became calamity—though it arose through men, it also touches the spirit principle.
translations.idiomatic: Baleful flames were secretly fanned and in a moment became calamity—though it arose through men, it also touches the spirit principle

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為火發既先從麻主，後及總章，意將所營佛舍，恐勞而無益。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the fire first started at the hemp master's quarters, then reached the Total Splendor hall—meaning the Buddha lodge under construction, feared labor without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thinks the fire first started at the hemp master's quarters, then reached Total Splendor—meaning the Buddha lodge under construction, labor without benefit.

sentences.zh: 但崇其教，即是津梁，何假紺宮，言存汲引？

translations.literal: Only honor the teaching—that itself is the ford; why need indigo palaces, speaking of drawing up water?
translations.idiomatic: Only honor the teaching—that itself is the ford; why need indigo palaces to draw up water?

sentences.zh: 既僻在明堂之後，又前逼牲牢之筵，兼以厥構崇大，功多難畢。

translations.literal: It stands secluded behind the Bright Hall and also presses close before the sacrificial beast pens—moreover its structure is lofty and great, the work many and hard to finish.
translations.idiomatic: It stands secluded behind the Bright Hall and presses before the sacrificial beast pens—moreover its structure is lofty, the work hard to finish.

sentences.zh: 立像弘法，本擬利益黎元，傷財役人，卻且煩勞家國。

translations.literal: Erecting images to spread the Law was originally meant to benefit the black-haired people; injuring wealth and conscripting men instead only wearies state and family.
translations.idiomatic: Erecting images to spread the Law was meant to benefit the people; injuring wealth and conscripting men instead wearies state and family.

sentences.zh: 承前大風摧木，天誡已顯；

translations.literal: Formerly the great wind toppled the timber—Heaven's admonition was already plain;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the great wind toppled the timber—Heaven's admonition was already plain;

sentences.zh: 今者毒焰冥熾，人孽復彰。

translations.literal: now poisonous flames burn darkly—human evil is again displayed.
translations.idiomatic: now poisonous flames burn darkly—human evil is again displayed

sentences.zh: 聖人動作，必假天人之助，一興功役，二者俱違，厥應昭然，殆將緣此。

translations.literal: The sage's movements must borrow the help of Heaven and man; once labor and conscription are raised, both are violated—the response is plain, and peril will likely follow from this.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's movements must borrow Heaven and man; once labor is raised, both are violated—the response is plain, and peril will likely follow.

sentences.zh: 臣以為明堂是正陽之位，至尊所居，展禮班常，崇化立政，玉帛朝會，神靈依憑。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the Bright Hall is the position of upright yang, where the Most High dwells—displaying ritual, ordering the constant, honoring transformation and establishing government; jade and silk assemblies, spirits relying upon it.
translations.idiomatic: thinks the Bright Hall is the position of upright yang, where the Most High dwells—displaying ritual, ordering the constant, honoring transformation and establishing government; jade and silk assemblies, spirits relying upon it.

sentences.zh: 營之可曰大功，損之實非輕事，既失嚴禋之所，復傷孝理之情。

translations.literal: To build it may be called a great achievement; to damage it is truly no light matter—having lost the place of solemn sacrifice, again injuring the feeling of filial principle.
translations.idiomatic: To build it is a great achievement; to damage it is no light matter—having lost the place of solemn sacrifice, again injuring filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 陛下昨降明制，猶申寅畏之旨，群僚理合兢畏震悚，勉力司存，豈合承恩耽樂，安然酺宴？

translations.literal: Your Majesty yesterday issued a bright edict still declaring the intent of reverent fear; the host of officials by reason ought to be reverent, alarmed, and trembling, striving in their offices—how should they accept favor, indulge in pleasure, and calmly feast?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty yesterday issued a bright edict still declaring reverent fear; officials ought to be alarmed and trembling, striving in office—how accept favor, indulge in pleasure, and calmly feast?

sentences.zh: 又下人感荷聖德，睹變憎惶，神體克寧，豈非深悅。

translations.literal: Moreover the people below, grateful for sage virtue, seeing the transformation are fearful and alarmed—the spirit body can be at peace; is this not deep joy?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the people below, grateful for sage virtue, seeing the transformation are fearful—the spirit body can be at peace; is this not deep joy?

sentences.zh: 但以火氣初止，尚多驚懼，餘憂未息，遽以歡事遏之。

translations.literal: But the fire's breath has only just ceased and alarm remains great; further worry has not subsided, yet suddenly joy affairs are used to check it.
translations.idiomatic: But the fire has only just ceased and alarm remains; further worry has not subsided, yet joy affairs are used to check it.

sentences.zh: 臣恐憂喜相爭，傷於情理。

translations.literal: Your servant fears worry and joy contending injures reason and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: fears worry and joy contending injures reason and feeling.

sentences.zh: 故傳曰：「可憂而為樂，取憂之道。

translations.literal: Thus the tradition says: "What should be worried about, yet made joy—that is the way to fetch worry."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says: "To make joy of what should worry you is the way to fetch worry."

sentences.zh: 」又古者有火，祭四墉。

translations.literal: Again in antiquity when there was fire, one sacrificed at the four embankments.
translations.idiomatic: in antiquity when there was fire, one sacrificed at the four embankments.

sentences.zh: 四墉，積陰之氣，祈之以禳火災。

translations.literal: The four embankments are accumulated yin qi; one prayed thereby to avert fire calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The four embankments are accumulated yin qi; one prayed thereby to avert fire.

sentences.zh: 火，陽之氣，歡樂陽事，火氣方勝，不可復興陽事。

translations.literal: Fire is yang qi; joy is a yang affair—when fire's qi is victorious, one cannot again raise a yang affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fire is yang qi— joy is a yang affair—when fire's qi is victorious, one cannot again raise a yang affair.

sentences.zh: 臣聞災變之興，至聖不免，聿修其德，來患可禳。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the rise of calamities and transformations—even the utmost sage does not escape; cultivate virtue and coming peril can be averted.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that calamities—even the utmost sage does not escape; cultivate virtue and coming peril can be averted.

sentences.zh: 陛下垂制博訪，許陳至理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty issued edicts broadly seeking counsel, permitting the utmost principle to be stated.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty issued edicts broadly seeking counsel, permitting the utmost principle to be stated

sentences.zh: 而左史張鼎以為「今既火流王屋，彌顯大周之祥」，通事舍人逢敏奏稱，「當彌勒初成佛道時，有天魔燒宮，七寶台須臾散壞。

translations.literal: Yet Left Historian Zhang Ding thought "now that fire flows through the king's house, it all the more displays Great Zhou's auspice," and Communications Gentleman Feng Min memorialized that "when Maitreya first achieved Buddhahood, heavenly demons burned the palace and the seven-jewel terrace was scattered in a moment."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Left Historian Zhang Ding thought "now that fire flows through the king's house, it all the more displays Great Zhou's auspice," and Communications Gentleman Feng Min said "when Maitreya first achieved Buddhahood, heavenly demons burned the palace and the seven-jewel terrace scattered in a moment."

sentences.zh: 」斯實諂妄之邪言，實非君臣之正論。

translations.literal: These are truly flattery and perverse words, truly not correct discourse between ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: These are flattery and perverse words, not correct discourse between ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 晻昧王化，無益萬機。

translations.literal: They dim kingly transformation and benefit not the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They dim kingly transformation and benefit not the myriad affairs

sentences.zh: 夫天道雖高，其察彌近；

translations.literal: Heaven's Way though high, its scrutiny is ever nearer;
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven's Way is high, its scrutiny draws ever nearer;

sentences.zh: 神心雖寂，其聽彌聰。

translations.literal: the spirit heart though still, its hearing is ever keener.
translations.idiomatic: the spirit heart though still, its hearing is ever keener

sentences.zh: 交際皇王，事均影響。

translations.literal: Their interchange with emperors and kings is like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: Their interchange with emperors and kings is like shadow and echo

sentences.zh: 今大風烈火，譴告相仍，實天人丁甯，匡諭聖主，便鴻基盆固，天祿永終之意也。

translations.literal: Now great wind and fierce fire, reprimand and admonition following in succession—truly Heaven and man admonishing and instructing the sage ruler, meaning that the great foundation grows ever firmer and Heaven's emolument endures forever.
translations.idiomatic: Now great wind and fierce fire, reprimand following in succession—truly Heaven and man admonishing the sage ruler, meaning the great foundation grows firmer and Heaven's emolument endures.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下乾乾在慮，翼翼為懷，若涉巨川，如承大祭，審其致災之理，詳其降眚之由，無瞢天人之心，而興不急之役。

translations.literal: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will be qianqian in thought, yiyi in heart, as if crossing a great stream, as if undertaking a great sacrifice—examine the reasons calamity was brought, detail the causes of descending reprimand, do not darken the heart toward Heaven and man, yet raise unurgent labor.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will be vigilant in thought, cautious in heart, as if crossing a great stream, as if undertaking a great sacrifice—examine why calamity came, detail the causes of reprimand, do not darken the heart toward Heaven and man, yet raise unurgent labor.

sentences.zh: 則兆人蒙賴，福祿靡窮，幸甚，幸甚。

translations.literal: Then the myriad people will rely upon you, fortune and emolument without end—most fortunate, most fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Then the myriad people will rely upon you, fortune without end—most fortunate, most fortunate.

sentences.zh: 則天尋令依舊規制重造明堂，凡高二百九十四尺，東西南北廣三百尺。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian shortly ordered the Bright Hall rebuilt according to the former regulations; in all it was two hundred ninety-four chi high, three hundred chi wide on east, south, west, and north.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian shortly ordered the Bright Hall rebuilt to former regulations; in all it was two hundred ninety-four chi high, three hundred chi wide on every side.

sentences.zh: 上施寶鳳，俄以火珠代之。

translations.literal: On top was set a jeweled phoenix; shortly a fire pearl replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: On top was set a jeweled phoenix— shortly a fire pearl replaced it.

sentences.zh: 明堂之下，圜饒施鐵渠，以為辟雍之象。

translations.literal: Below the Bright Hall, a circular moat with iron channels was laid, as the image of the Ring Moat.
translations.idiomatic: Below the Bright Hall, a circular moat with iron channels was laid, as the image of the Ring Moat

sentences.zh: 天冊萬歲二年三月，重造明堂成，號為通天宮。

translations.literal: In the third month of Tianche Wansui year 2, the Bright Hall was rebuilt and completed, titled the Hall of Piercing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianche Wansui year 2, the Bright Hall was rebuilt and completed, titled the Hall of Piercing Heaven

sentences.zh: 四月朔日，又行親享之禮，大赦，改元為萬歲通天。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, the personal offering rite was again performed, a great amnesty proclaimed, and the era name changed to Wansui Tongtian.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, the personal offering was again performed, a great amnesty proclaimed, and the era changed to Wansui Tongtian.

sentences.zh: 翼日，則天禦通天宮之端扆殿，命有司讀時令，布政於群後。

translations.literal: The next day, Wu Zetian attended the Screen Hall of the Hall of Piercing Heaven, ordered the responsible offices to read the seasonal ordinances, and dispensed government to the host of nobles.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, Wu Zetian attended the Screen Hall of the Hall of Piercing Heaven, ordered the offices to read the seasonal ordinances, and dispensed government to the nobles.

sentences.zh: 其年，鑄銅為九州鼎，既成，置於明堂之庭，各依方位列焉。

translations.literal: That year, bronze was cast into the Nine Provinces cauldrons; when completed, they were placed in the Bright Hall courtyard, each arrayed by its directional position.
translations.idiomatic: That year bronze was cast into the Nine Provinces cauldrons; when completed, they were placed in the Bright Hall courtyard, each arrayed by direction.

sentences.zh: 神都鼎高一丈八尺，受一千八百石。

translations.literal: The Divine Capital cauldron was one zhang eight chi high and held one thousand eight hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Divine Capital cauldron was one zhang eight chi high and held one thousand eight hundred shi

sentences.zh: 冀州鼎名武興，雍州鼎名長安，兗州名日觀，青州名少陽，徐州名東原，揚州名江都，荊州名江陵，梁州名成都。

translations.literal: The Jizhou cauldron was named Martial Flourishing, Yongzhou cauldron Long Peace, Yanzhou cauldron Sun Vista, Qingzhou cauldron Lesser Yang, Xuzhou cauldron Eastern Plain, Yangzhou cauldron River Capital, Jingzhou cauldron River Mound, Liangzhou cauldron Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jizhou cauldron was named Martial Flourishing, Yongzhou Long Peace, Yanzhou Sun Vista, Qingzhou Lesser Yang, Xuzhou Eastern Plain, Yangzhou River Capital, Jingzhou River Mound, Liangzhou Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 其八州鼎高一丈四尺，各受一千二百石。

translations.literal: The eight provincial cauldrons were one zhang four chi high, each holding one thousand two hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: The eight provincial cauldrons were one zhang four chi high, each holding one thousand two hundred shi

sentences.zh: 司農卿宗晉卿為九鼎使，都用銅五十六萬七百一十二斤。

translations.literal: Director of Agriculture Zong Jinqing was made commissioner of the Nine Cauldrons; in all five hundred sixty thousand seven hundred twelve jin of copper were used.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Agriculture Zong Jinqing was made commissioner of the Nine Cauldrons— in all five hundred sixty thousand seven hundred twelve jin of copper were used.

sentences.zh: 鼎上圖寫本州山川物產之像，仍令工書人著作郎賈膺福、殿中丞薛昌容、鳳閣主事李元振、司農錄事鐘紹京等分題之，左尚方署令曹元廓圖畫之。

translations.literal: On the cauldrons were painted the mountains, rivers, and products of each province; Writing Gentleman of the Works Office Jia Yingfu, Palace Administration Vice Director Xue Changrong, Phoenix Pavilion Principal Clerk Li Yuanzhen, Agriculture Office Recorder Zhong Shaojing, and others were ordered to inscribe the titles separately; Left Palace Workshop Office Director Cao Yuanlang painted the designs.
translations.idiomatic: On the cauldrons were painted each province's mountains, rivers, and products; Jia Yingfu, Xue Changrong, Li Yuanzhen, Zhong Shaojing, and others inscribed titles; Cao Yuanlang painted the designs.

sentences.zh: 鼎成，自玄武門外曳入，令宰相、諸王率南北衙宿衛兵十余萬人，並仗內大牛、白象共曳之。

translations.literal: When the cauldrons were completed, they were dragged in from outside the Dark Warrior Gate; chancellors and kings of various ranks led more than a hundred thousand northern and southern Yamen guard soldiers, together with great oxen and white elephants from within the guard, to drag them together.
translations.idiomatic: When the cauldrons were completed, they were dragged in from outside the Dark Warrior Gate; chancellors and kings led more than a hundred thousand guard soldiers, with great oxen and white elephants from the inner guard, to drag them together.

sentences.zh: 則天自為《曳鼎歌》，令相唱和。

translations.literal: Wu Zetian herself composed the "Dragging Cauldron Song" and ordered ministers to sing in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zetian herself composed the "Dragging Cauldron Song" and ordered ministers to sing in response

sentences.zh: 其時又造大儀鐘，斂天下三品金，竟不成。

translations.literal: At that time a great ceremonial bell was also made, gathering gold of the third rank from all under Heaven—it was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a great ceremonial bell was also made, gathering third-rank gold from all under Heaven—it was never completed.

sentences.zh: 九鼎初成，欲以黃金千兩塗之。

translations.literal: When the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, it was wished to gild them with a thousand liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine Cauldrons were first completed, it was wished to gild them with a thousand liang of gold

sentences.zh: 納言姚璹曰：「鼎者神器，貴于質樸，無假別為浮飾。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yao Shuang said: "Cauldrons are spirit vessels; they are honored for plain substance, with no need to make separate floating ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yao Shuang said: "Cauldrons are spirit vessels; they are honored for plain substance, with no need for floating ornament.

sentences.zh: 臣觀其狀，光有五彩輝煥錯雜其間，豈待金色為之炫耀？

translations.literal: Your servant observes their form—light of five colors, brilliant and interwoven among them; why wait for gold color to make them dazzle?"
translations.idiomatic: Your servant observes their form—light of five colors, brilliant and interwoven; why wait for gold to dazzle?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was stopped

sentences.zh: 其年九月，又大享於通天宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, the great offering was again performed at the Hall of Piercing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year, the great offering was again performed at the Hall of Piercing Heaven

sentences.zh: 以契丹破滅，九鼎初成，大赦。

translations.literal: Because the Khitan were destroyed and the Nine Cauldrons newly completed, a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Khitan were destroyed and the Nine Cauldrons newly completed, a great amnesty was proclaimed

sentences.zh: 改元為神功。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Divine Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Divine Achievement

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年正月，又親享及受朝賀。

translations.literal: In the first month of Shenglü year 1, the personal offering and receiving court congratulations were again performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Shenglü year 1, the personal offering and court congratulations were again performed.

sentences.zh: 尋制：每月一日於明堂行告朔之禮。

translations.literal: Shortly an ordinance was made: on the first day of each month perform the announcing-new-moon rite at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly an ordinance was made: on the first day of each month perform the announcing-new-moon rite at the Bright Hall

sentences.zh: 司禮博士辟閭仁諝奏議曰：

translations.literal: Ritual Office Erudite Pilu Renxu submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Pilu Renxu submitted a deliberation, :

sentences.zh: 謹按經史正文，無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the canonical texts of classics and histories, there is no affair of the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully per classics and histories, there is no Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.

sentences.zh: 惟《禮記·玉藻》云：「天子聽朔于南門之外。

translations.literal: Only the Record of Rites, Jade Regalia, says: "The Son of Heaven hears the new moon outside the southern gate."
translations.idiomatic: the Record of Rites, Jade Regalia, says: "The Son of Heaven hears the new moon outside the southern gate."

sentences.zh: 」《周禮·天官·太宰》：「正月之吉，布政于邦國都鄙。

translations.literal: The Zhou Offices, Heavenly Offices, Grand Steward: "On the auspicious day of the first month, dispense government to the states, capitals, and districts."
translations.idiomatic: the Zhou Offices, Heavenly Offices, Grand Steward: "On the auspicious day of the first month, dispense government to the states, capitals, and districts."

sentences.zh: 」幹寶注云：「周正建子之月，告朔日也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's note says: "The Zhou calendar beginning in the zi month—the day of announcing the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao notes: "The Zhou calendar beginning in the zi month—the day of announcing the new moon."

sentences.zh: 」此即《玉藻》之聽朔矣。

translations.literal: This is the hearing the new moon of Jade Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: This is the hearing the new moon of Jade Regalia

sentences.zh: 今每歲首元日，於通天宮受朝，讀時令，布政事，京官九品以上、諸州朝集使等咸列於庭，此則聽朔之禮畢，而合于《周禮》、《玉藻》之文矣。

translations.literal: Now each year on New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven court is received, seasonal ordinances read, government dispensed—capital officials of the ninth rank and above and gathering envoys from the prefectures all stand in the court: this completes the hearing-the-new-moon rite and accords with the texts of Zhou Offices and Jade Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Now each New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven court is received, ordinances read, government dispensed—capital officials of the ninth rank and above and gathering envoys all stand in court: this completes hearing the new moon and accords with Zhou Offices and Jade Regalia.

sentences.zh: 而鄭玄注《玉藻》「聽朔」，以秦制月令有五帝五官之事，遂云：「凡聽朔，必特牲告其時帝及其神，配以文王、武王。

translations.literal: Yet Zheng Xuan's note on Jade Regalia "hearing the new moon," because Qin institutions' monthly ordinances had the Five Emperors and Five Official Spirits affair, thus says: "Whenever hearing the new moon, one must use a special victim to announce that month's Emperor and its spirit, matching King Wen and King Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zheng Xuan's note on "hearing the new moon," because Qin monthly ordinances had Five Emperors and Five Official Spirits, says: "Whenever hearing the new moon, use a special victim to announce that month's Emperor and spirit, matching King Wen and King Wu."

sentences.zh: 」此鄭注之誤也。

translations.literal: This is Zheng's erroneous note.
translations.idiomatic: This is Zheng's error.

sentences.zh: 故漢魏至今莫之用。

translations.literal: Thus from Han and Wei to the present none have used it.
