translations.idiomatic: from Han and Wei to the present none have used it.

sentences.zh: 按《月令》雲「其帝太昊，其神勾芒」者，謂宣佈時令，告示下人，其令詞雲其帝其神耳。

translations.literal: Per the Monthly Ordinances saying "its Emperor Taihao, its spirit Goumang"—that means announcing seasonal ordinances, informing those below; the ordinance words say its Emperor, its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Per the Monthly Ordinances saying "its Emperor Taihao, its spirit Goumang"—that means announcing seasonal ordinances to those below; the ordinance words say its Emperor, its spirit.

sentences.zh: 所以為敬授之文，欲使人奉其時而務其業。

translations.literal: Therefore it is respectful granting text, wishing to make people observe the season and attend to their work.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is respectful granting text, wishing people to observe the season and attend to their work.

sentences.zh: 每月有令，故謂之《月令》，非謂天子月朔日以祖配帝而察告之。

translations.literal: Each month has an ordinance, hence it is called Monthly Ordinances—not meaning that on the Son of Heaven's monthly new-moon day he matches ancestors to Emperors and inspects and announces.
translations.idiomatic: Each month has an ordinance, hence Monthly Ordinances—not that on the Son of Heaven's new-moon day he matches ancestors to Emperors and announces.

sentences.zh: 其每月告朔者，諸候之禮也。

translations.literal: The monthly announcing of the new moon is the rite of feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The monthly announcing of the new moon is the rite of feudal lords

sentences.zh: 故《春秋左氏傳》曰：「公既視朔，遂登觀台。

translations.literal: Thus the Zuo Commentary says: "The duke having already viewed the new moon, thereupon ascended the observation terrace."
translations.idiomatic: the Zuo Commentary says: "The duke having already viewed the new moon, then ascended the observation terrace."

sentences.zh: 」又鄭注《論語》云：「禮，人君每月告朔於廟，有祭謂之朝享。

translations.literal: Again Zheng's note on the Analects: "Ritual: the lord each month announces the new moon at the temple; if there is sacrifice it is called court offering.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's note on the Analects: "Ritual: the lord each month announces the new moon at the temple; if there is sacrifice it is called court offering.

sentences.zh: 魯自文公始不視朔。

translations.literal: Lu from Duke Wen onward ceased viewing the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: lu from Duke Wen onward ceased viewing the new moon."

sentences.zh: 」是諸候之禮明矣。

translations.literal: Thus the feudal lords' rite is clear.
translations.idiomatic: the feudal lords' rite is clear.

sentences.zh: 今王者行之，非所聞也。

translations.literal: Now for the king to perform it is unheard of.
translations.idiomatic: Now for the king to perform it is unheard of

sentences.zh: 按鄭所謂告其帝者即太昊等五人帝，其神者即重黎等五行官。

translations.literal: Per Zheng's so-called announcing to the Emperors—that is Taihao and the other five Emperor spirits; the spirits are Chongli and the other Five Phase officials.
translations.idiomatic: Per Zheng's announcing to the Emperors—that is Taihao and the other five; the spirits are Chongli and the other Five Phase officials.

sentences.zh: 雖並功施於人，列在祀典，無天子每月拜祭告朔之文。

translations.literal: Though their achievements benefited people and they are listed in the sacrifice canon, there is no text of the Son of Heaven bowing and sacrificing and announcing the new moon each month.
translations.idiomatic: Though their achievements benefited people and they are in the sacrifice canon, there is no Son of Heaven bowing and announcing the new moon each month.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹檢《禮論》及《三禮義宗》、《江都集禮》、《貞觀禮》、《顯慶禮》及祠令，並無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: Your servants respectfully examined Ritual Discussions, Three Rites Meaning Summaries, Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances—nowhere is there the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants examined Ritual Discussions, Three Rites Meaning Summaries, Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances—nowhere the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.

sentences.zh: 若以為代無明堂，故無告朔之禮，則《江都集禮》、《貞觀禮》、《顯慶禮》及祠令，著祀五方上帝於明堂，即《孝經》「宗祀文王於明堂」也。

translations.literal: If one thinks that because there was no Bright Hall in the age there was no announcing-new-moon rite, then Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances record sacrificing to the Five Directional High Gods at the Bright Hall—that is the Classic of Filial Piety's "zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall."
translations.idiomatic: If one thinks no Bright Hall meant no announcing-new-moon rite, then Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances record Five Directional High Gods at the Bright Hall—the Classic of Filial Piety's "zong sacrifice to King Wen at the Bright Hall."

sentences.zh: 此則無明堂而著其享祭，何為告朔獨闕其文？

translations.literal: Thus without Bright Hall the offering sacrifice is recorded—why alone is announcing the new moon missing from the text?
translations.idiomatic: Thus without Bright Hall the offering is recorded—why alone is announcing the new moon missing?

sentences.zh: 若以君有明堂即合告朔，則周、秦有明堂，而經典正文，無天子每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: If one thinks that when the ruler has a Bright Hall he should announce the new moon, then Zhou and Qin had Bright Halls, yet canonical texts nowhere have the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.
translations.idiomatic: If when the ruler has a Bright Hall he should announce the new moon, Zhou and Qin had Bright Halls, yet canonical texts nowhere have the Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month.

sentences.zh: 臣等曆觀今古，博考載籍，既無其禮，不可習非。

translations.literal: Your servants have examined past and present through the ages, broadly consulted records—since there is no rite, one cannot practice error.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants have examined past and present, broadly consulted records—since there is no rite, one cannot practice error.

sentences.zh: 望請停每月一日告朔之祭，以正國經。

translations.literal: We hope the monthly first-day announcing-new-moon sacrifice may be stopped to rectify the state canon.
translations.idiomatic: We hope the monthly first-day announcing-new-moon sacrifice may be stopped to rectify the state canon

sentences.zh: 竊以天子之尊，而用諸侯之禮，非所謂頒告朔、令諸侯、使奉而行之之義也。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks the Son of Heaven's dignity using feudal lords' rite is not what is meant by issuing announced new moon to feudal lords and making them receive and perform it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thinks the Son of Heaven's dignity using feudal lords' rite is not what is meant by issuing announced new moon to feudal lords for them to perform.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣侍郎王方慶又奏議曰：

translations.literal: Phoenix Pavilion Vice Director Wang Fangqing also submitted a deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Fangqing also submitted a deliberation, :

sentences.zh: 謹按明堂，天子布政之宮也。

translations.literal: Respectfully per the Bright Hall—it is the Son of Heaven's palace for dispensing government.
translations.idiomatic: per the Bright Hall—it is the Son of Heaven's palace for dispensing government.

sentences.zh: 蓋所以順天氣，統萬物，動法於兩儀，德被于四海者也。

translations.literal: Broadly it is to accord with Heaven's qi, order the myriad things, move taking the Two Modes as model, virtue covering the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly it accords with Heaven's qi, orders the myriad things, moves taking the Two Modes as model, virtue covering the four seas.

sentences.zh: 夏曰世室，殷曰重屋，姬曰明堂，此三代之名也。

translations.literal: Xia called it Generations Chamber, Yin called it Layered Roof, Ji called it Bright Hall—these are the three dynasties' names.
translations.idiomatic: Xia called it Generations Chamber, Yin Layered Roof, Zhou Bright Hall—the names of three dynasties.

sentences.zh: 明堂，天子太廟，所以宗祀其祖，以配上帝。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is the Son of Heaven's Grand Temple, whereby he zong-sacrifices his ancestors, matching the High God.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is the Son of Heaven's Grand Temple, whereby he zong-sacrifices his ancestors, matching the High God

sentences.zh: 東曰青陽，南曰明堂，西曰總章，北曰玄堂，中曰太室。

translations.literal: East is Azure Yang, south Bright Hall, west Total Splendor, north Dark Hall, center Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: East is Azure Yang, south Bright Hall, west Total Splendor, north Dark Hall, center Grand Chamber

sentences.zh: 雖有五名，而以明堂為主。

translations.literal: Though there are five names, Bright Hall is taken as primary.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are five names, Bright Hall is primary.

sentences.zh: 漢代達學通儒，鹹以明堂、太廟為一。

translations.literal: Han dynasty accomplished scholars and penetrating ru all took Bright Hall and Grand Temple as one.
translations.idiomatic: Han accomplished scholars and penetrating ru all took Bright Hall and Grand Temple as one.

sentences.zh: 漢左中郎將蔡邕立議，亦以為然。

translations.literal: Han Left Palace Gentleman Cai Yong established the deliberation, also holding it so.
translations.idiomatic: Han Left Palace Gentleman Cai Yong established the deliberation, also holding it so

sentences.zh: 取其宗祀，則謂之清廟；

translations.literal: Taking its zong sacrifice, it is called Pure Temple;
translations.idiomatic: taking its zong sacrifice, it is called Pure Temple;

sentences.zh: 取其正室，則謂之太室；

translations.literal: taking its main chamber, it is called Grand Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: as main chamber, it is called Grand Chamber;

sentences.zh: 取其向陽，則謂之明堂；

translations.literal: taking its facing the sun, it is called Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: as the sun-facing hall, it is called Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 取其建學，則謂之太學；

translations.literal: taking its establishing study, it is called Grand Academy;
translations.idiomatic: as the place of learning, it is called Grand Academy;

sentences.zh: 取其圜水，則謂之辟雍。

translations.literal: taking its circular water, it is called Ring Moat.
translations.idiomatic: taking its circular water, it is called Ring Moat

sentences.zh: 異名而同事，古之制也。

translations.literal: Different names, same affair—antiquity's institution.
translations.idiomatic: Different names, same affair—antiquity's institution

sentences.zh: 天子以孟春正月上辛日，於南郊總受十二月之政，還藏于祖廟，月取一政班於明堂。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven on the first xin day of the first month of early spring at the southern suburb altogether receives the twelve months' government, returns and stores it in the ancestral temple, each month taking one government and issuing it at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven on the first xin day of early spring at the southern suburb receives the twelve months' government, returns and stores it in the ancestral temple, each month taking one government and issuing it at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 諸侯孟春之月，朝于天子，受十二月之政藏于祖廟，月取一政而行之。

translations.literal: Feudal lords in the early-spring month attend the Son of Heaven, receive the twelve months' government and store it in the ancestral temple, each month taking one government and performing it.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords in early spring attend the Son of Heaven, receive the twelve months' government and store it in the ancestral temple, each month taking one government and performing it.

sentences.zh: 蓋所以和陰陽、順天道也。

translations.literal: Broadly this harmonizes yin and yang and accords with Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly this harmonizes yin and yang and accords with Heaven's Way

sentences.zh: 如此則禍亂不作，災害不生矣。

translations.literal: Thus calamity and disorder do not arise, disasters and harms are not born.
translations.idiomatic: Thus calamity and disorder do not arise, disasters are not born.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼美而稱之曰：「明王之以孝理天下也。

translations.literal: Thus Confucius beautifully praised it, saying: "The enlightened king uses filial piety to order all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Thus Confucius praised it beautifully: "The enlightened king uses filial piety to order all under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」人君以其禮告廟，則謂之告朔；

translations.literal: The lord announcing ritual at the temple is called announcing the new moon;
translations.idiomatic: the lord announcing ritual at the temple is called announcing the new moon;

sentences.zh: 聽視此月之政，則謂之視朔，亦曰聽朔。

translations.literal: hearing and viewing that month's government is called viewing the new moon, also called hearing the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: hearing and viewing that month's government is called viewing the new moon, also hearing the new moon.

sentences.zh: 雖有三名，其實一也。

translations.literal: Though there are three names, the substance is one.
translations.idiomatic: Though there are three names, the substance is one

sentences.zh: 今禮官議稱「經史正文無天子每月告朔之事」者。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officers' deliberation says "canonical texts of classics and histories have no Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month."
translations.idiomatic: Now the ritual officers say "canonical texts have no Son of Heaven announcing the new moon each month."

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《春秋》：「文公六年閏十月，不告朔。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully per the Spring and Autumn: "Duke Wen year 6, intercalary tenth month—did not announce the new moon."
translations.idiomatic: respectfully per the Spring and Autumn: "Duke Wen year 6, intercalary tenth month—did not announce the new moon."

sentences.zh: 」《谷梁傳》曰：「閏，附月之余日，天子不以告朔。

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: "Intercalation is the month's surplus days; the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon for it."
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: "Intercalation is the month's surplus days— the Son of Heaven does not announce the new moon for it."

sentences.zh: 」《左氏傳》云：「閏月不告朔，非禮也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "Not announcing intercalary new moon is uncanonical.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "Not announcing intercalary new moon is uncanonical

sentences.zh: 閏以正時，時以作事，事以厚生，生人之道，於是乎在矣。

translations.literal: Intercalation corrects the seasons; seasons make affairs; affairs thicken life—the way of the living is therein.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalation corrects the seasons— seasons make affairs— affairs thicken life—the way of the living is therein.

sentences.zh: 不告閏朔，棄時政也。

translations.literal: Not announcing intercalary new moon abandons seasonal government."
translations.idiomatic: not announcing intercalary new moon abandons seasonal government."

sentences.zh: 」臣據此文，則天子閏月亦告朔矣。

translations.literal: By this text of your servant, the Son of Heaven also announces new moon in intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: By this text, the Son of Heaven also announces new moon in intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 寧有他月而廢其禮者乎？

translations.literal: How could there be other months while abandoning the rite?
translations.idiomatic: how could there be other months while abandoning the rite?

sentences.zh: 博考經籍，其文甚著。

translations.literal: Broadly examining classics and histories, the text is very plain.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly examining classics and histories, the text is very plain

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is it clear?
translations.idiomatic: how is it clear?

sentences.zh: 《周禮·太史》職云：「頒告朔于邦國。

translations.literal: Zhou Offices, Grand Clerk's duty: "Issue announced new moon to the states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Offices, Grand Clerk's duty: "Issue announced new moon to the states

sentences.zh: 閏月，告王居門終月。

translations.literal: Intercalary month—announce to the king dwelling at the gate for the full month."
translations.idiomatic: intercalary month—announce to the king dwelling at the gate for the full month."

sentences.zh: 」又《禮記·玉藻》云：「閏月則合門左扉，立於其中。

translations.literal: Again Record of Rites, Jade Regalia: "In intercalary month close the gate's left leaf and stand within it."
translations.idiomatic: Record of Rites, Jade Regalia: "In intercalary month close the gate's left leaf and stand within it."

sentences.zh: 」並是天子閏月而行告朔之事也。

translations.literal: Both are the Son of Heaven performing announcing-new-moon affairs in intercalary months.
translations.idiomatic: Both are the Son of Heaven performing announcing-new-moon affairs in intercalary months

sentences.zh: 禮官又稱：「《玉藻》，'天子聽朔于南門之外。

translations.literal: The ritual officers also say: "Jade Regalia, 'the Son of Heaven hears the new moon outside the southern gate.'
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officers say: "Jade Regalia, 'the Son of Heaven hears the new moon outside the southern gate.'

sentences.zh: '《周禮·天官·太宰》，'正月之吉，布政于邦國都鄙。

translations.literal: Zhou Offices, Heavenly Offices, Grand Steward, 'on the auspicious day of the first month, dispense government to the states, capitals, and districts.'
translations.idiomatic: zhou Offices, Heavenly Offices, Grand Steward, 'on the auspicious day of the first month, dispense government to the states, capitals, and districts.'

sentences.zh: '幹寶注雲，'周正建子之月，告朔日也。

translations.literal: Gan Bao's note says, 'the Zhou calendar beginning in the zi month is the day of announcing the new moon.'
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao notes, 'the Zhou calendar beginning in the zi month is the day of announcing the new moon.'

sentences.zh: '此即《玉藻》之聽朔矣。

translations.literal: This is Jade Regalia's hearing the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: This is Jade Regalia's hearing the new moon

sentences.zh: 今每歲首元日，通天宮受朝，讀時令，布政事，京官九品以上、諸州朝集使等咸列於庭，此聽朔之禮畢，而合于《周禮》、《玉藻》之文矣。

translations.literal: Now each year on New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven court is received, seasonal ordinances read, government dispensed—capital officials of the ninth rank and above and gathering envoys from the prefectures all stand in the court: this completes the hearing-the-new-moon rite and accords with the texts of Zhou Offices and Jade Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Now each New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven court is received, ordinances read, government dispensed—officials of the ninth rank and above and gathering envoys stand in court: this completes hearing the new moon and accords with Zhou Offices and Jade Regalia.

sentences.zh: 《禮論》及《三禮義宗》、《江都集禮》、《貞觀禮》、《顯慶禮》及祠令，無王者告朔之事者。

translations.literal: Ritual Discussions, Three Rites Meaning Summaries, Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances have no affair of the king announcing the new moon.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual Discussions, Three Rites Meaning Summaries, Jiangdu Collected Rites, Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrifice ordinances have no king announcing the new moon.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按《玉藻雲》：「玄冕而朝日於東門之外，聽朔于南門之外。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully per Jade Regalia: "Dark regalia and attend the sun at the eastern gate outside, hear the new moon at the southern gate outside."
translations.idiomatic: respectfully per Jade Regalia: "Dark regalia and attend the sun at the eastern gate outside, hear the new moon at the southern gate outside."

sentences.zh: 」鄭注云：「朝日，春分之時也。

translations.literal: Zheng's note says: "Attending the sun is at the time of the spring equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng notes: "Attending the sun is at the spring equinox.

sentences.zh: 東門、南門，皆謂國門也。

translations.literal: Eastern gate and southern gate both mean the state gate."
translations.idiomatic: The eastern and southern gates both mean the state gate."

sentences.zh: 明堂在國之陽，每月就其時之堂而聽朔焉，卒事，反宿于路寢。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is in the state's yang; each month one goes to that season's hall to hear the new moon; when the affair is finished, one returns to lodge at the Road Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is in the state's yang; each month one goes to that season's hall to hear the new moon; when finished, one returns to lodge at the Road Chamber.

sentences.zh: 凡聽朔，必以特牲告其時帝及其神，配以文王、武王。

translations.literal: Whenever hearing the new moon, one must use a special victim to announce that month's Emperor and its spirit, matching King Wen and King Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever hearing the new moon, one must use a special victim to announce that month's Emperor and spirit, matching King Wen and King Wu."

sentences.zh: 」臣謂今歲首元日，通天宮受朝，讀時令及布政，自是古禮孟春上辛，受十二月之政藏于祖廟之禮耳，而月取一政，班於明堂，其義昭然，猶未行也。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that now on New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven receiving court, reading seasonal ordinances and dispensing government is itself the ancient rite of early spring first xin receiving the twelve months' government and storing it in the ancestral temple—but taking one government each month and issuing it at the Bright Hall, though the meaning is plain, it is still not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant thinks New Year's Day at the Hall of Piercing Heaven receiving court, reading ordinances and dispensing government is the ancient early-spring first xin rite of receiving twelve months' government and storing it in the ancestral temple—but taking one government monthly at the Bright Hall, though plain in meaning, is still not performed.

sentences.zh: 即如禮官所言，遂闕其事。

translations.literal: If one follows what the ritual officers say, that affair is then lacking.
translations.idiomatic: If one follows the ritual officers, that affair is then lacking.

sentences.zh: 臣又按《禮記·月令》，天子每月居青陽、明堂、總章、玄堂，即是每月告朔之事。

translations.literal: Your servant further examines the Record of Rites, "Monthly Ordinances": each month the Son of Heaven dwells in Azure Yang, Bright Hall, Total Splendor, and Dark Hall—that is the affair of monthly gaosu.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further notes the Record of Rites, "Monthly Ordinances": each month the Son of Heaven dwells in Azure Yang, Bright Hall, Total Splendor, and Dark Hall—the monthly gaosu rite.

sentences.zh: 先儒舊說，天子行事，一年十八度入明堂：大享不問卜，一入也；

translations.literal: Former scholars' old doctrine: in conducting affairs the Son of Heaven enters the Bright Hall eighteen times in a year—the great sacrifice without divination, one entry;
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars held that in a year the Son of Heaven entered the Bright Hall eighteen times: the great sacrifice without divination, once;

sentences.zh: 每月告朔，十二入也；

translations.literal: monthly gaosu, twelve entries;
translations.idiomatic: monthly gaosu, twelve times;

sentences.zh: 四時迎氣，四入也；

translations.literal: the four seasons welcoming the qi, four entries;
translations.idiomatic: welcoming the qi of the four seasons, four times;

sentences.zh: 巡狩之年，一入也。

translations.literal: in years of the imperial tour of inspection, one entry.
translations.idiomatic: in years of the imperial tour, once.

sentences.zh: 今禮官立義，王惟歲首一入耳，與先儒既異，臣不敢同。

translations.literal: Now the ritual officials establish the doctrine that the king enters only once at the year's head—already differing from former scholars; your servant dare not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Today the ritualists hold that the king enters only at the year's head—at odds with the old masters. Your servant cannot agree.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「凡聽朔告其帝。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Whenever hearing the new moon, announce to its Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "Whenever the court hears the new moon, it announces to that season's Thearch.

sentences.zh: 」臣愚以為告朔之日，則五方上帝之一帝也。

translations.literal: " Your servant foolishly holds that on the gaosu day it is one of the Five Directional High Gods.
translations.idiomatic: " Your servant holds that on gaosu day it is one of the Five Directional High Gods.

sentences.zh: 春則靈威仰，夏則赤熛怒，秋則白招拒，冬則葉光紀，季月則含樞紐也，並以始祖而配之焉。

translations.literal: In spring then Spiritual Power Uplifted; in summer Blazing Fury; in autumn White Summoner Repelled; in winter Radiant Light Eras; in the season's last month then Pivot Token—all with the founding ancestor as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Spring: Spiritual Power Uplifted; summer: Blazing Fury; autumn: White Summoner Repelled; winter: Radiant Light Eras; the season's last month: Pivot Token—each with the founding ancestor as consort.

sentences.zh: 人帝及神，列在祀典，亦於其月而享祭之。

translations.literal: Human Thearchs and spirits, listed in the sacrificial canon, are also offered sacrifice in their months.
translations.idiomatic: The human Thearchs and spirits in the sacrificial canon receive offerings in their proper months.

sentences.zh: 魯自文公始不視朔，子貢見其禮廢，欲去其羊，孔子以羊存猶可識其禮，羊亡其禮遂廢，故云：「爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: Lu from Duke Wen onward did not view the new moon; Zigong saw its rite abandoned and wished to remove the sheep; Confucius held that while the sheep remained the rite could still be known, but with the sheep gone the rite was utterly abandoned—thus he said: "You love the sheep; I love the rite.
translations.idiomatic: From Duke Wen of Lu the state ceased viewing the new moon. Zigong saw the rite fall into ruin and wanted to abolish the sacrificial sheep. Confucius said that while the sheep remained one could still recognize the rite; without the sheep the rite was lost. Hence: "You love your sheep; I love the rite.

translations.literal: The quotation concluded."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects quote ended.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦滅學，庶事草創，明堂、辟雍，其制遂闕。

translations.literal: Han, inheriting Qin's destruction of learning, began all affairs from scratch; Bright Hall and Imperial Academy—their institutions were wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose after Qin burned the schools; every institution was new. Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were never properly built.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝封禪，始造明堂於太山，既不立于京師，所以無告朔之事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's feng and shan first built a Bright Hall at Mount Tai; since it was not established in the capital, there were no gaosu affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's feng and shan raised a Bright Hall on Mount Tai—but not in the capital, so there was no gaosu.

sentences.zh: 至漢平帝元始中，王莽輔政，庶幾復古，乃建明堂、辟雍焉。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ping's Yuanshi era Wang Mang assisted government and nearly restored antiquity—then built Bright Hall and Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ping, in the Yuanshi era, Wang Mang governed and sought to restore antiquity; he built Bright Hall and Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝祫祭於明堂，諸侯王、列侯、宗室子弟九百餘人助祭畢，皆益戶、賜爵及金帛、增秩、補吏各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor performed the collective autumn sacrifice at the Bright Hall; feudal kings, marquises, and over nine hundred imperial clansmen assisted at sacrifice's end—all received household augmentation, enfeoffment of rank, gold and silk, promotion in rank, and appointment as officials, each in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor performed the collective autumn rite at the Bright Hall. More than nine hundred feudal kings, marquises, and clansmen assisted; when the rite ended each was rewarded—households enlarged, ranks granted, gold and silk bestowed, promotions and appointments, all by degree.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，尚傳其禮。

translations.literal: At Han's end turmoil reigned, yet the rite was still transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Han ended in chaos, yet the rite still passed down.

sentences.zh: 爰至後漢，祀典仍存。

translations.literal: Down to Later Han the sacrificial canon still endured.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Han the sacrificial canon remained.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平二年，郊祀五帝於明堂，以光武配，祭牲各一犢，奏樂如南郊。

translations.literal: In Mingdi's Yongping year 2, suburban sacrifice to the Five Thearchs at the Bright Hall with Guangwu as consort—each offering one calf, music as at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping year 2 of Mingdi: the Five Thearchs were sacrificed at the Bright Hall in the suburbs, with Guangwu as consort—one calf each, music as at the southern altar.

sentences.zh: 董卓西移，載籍湮滅，告朔之禮，於此而墜。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo's westward move extinguished records; the gaosu rite fell here.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's flight westward drowned the archives; the gaosu rite collapsed here.

sentences.zh: 暨于晉末，其馬生郊，禮樂衣冠，掃地總盡。

translations.literal: By Jin's end "its horses were born in the suburbs"—ritual, music, caps and robes swept utterly away.
translations.idiomatic: By Jin's end—"horses born in the suburbs"—ritual, music, caps and robes were swept away entirely.

sentences.zh: 元帝過江，是稱狼狽，禮樂制度，南遷蓋寡，彝曲殘缺，無復舊章，軍國所資，臨事議之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan crossing the river was called a sorry scramble; ritual and music institutions southward migrated mostly sparse; canonical tunes were mutilated with no old statutes revived; what army and state needed was decided as affairs arose.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan fled south in disarray; ritual and music crossed the river only in fragments. Canonical melodies were broken; old statutes did not return. What army and state required was improvised as events demanded.

sentences.zh: 既闕明堂，寧論告朔。

translations.literal: With the Bright Hall lacking, how discuss gaosu?
translations.idiomatic: Without a Bright Hall, who could speak of gaosu?

sentences.zh: 宋朝何承天纂集其文，以為《禮論》，雖加編次，事則闕如。

translations.literal: Song's He Chengtian compiled texts into Discourses on Rites—though arranged, the affairs were wanting.
translations.idiomatic: In Song, He Chengtian compiled texts into Discourses on Rites—well ordered, but the substance was missing.

sentences.zh: 梁代崔靈恩撰《三禮義宗》，更無異文。

translations.literal: Liang's Cui Lingen wrote Notes on the Meaning of the Three Rites with no differing text.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, Cui Lingen's Notes on the Meaning of the Three Rites added nothing new.

sentences.zh: 《貞觀》、《顯慶禮》及祠令不言告朔者，蓋為歷代不傳，其文遂闕，各有由緒，不足依據。

translations.literal: Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and sacrificial ordinances not speaking of gaosu—likely because successive ages did not transmit it, the text was wanting; each had its reasons and cannot serve as basis.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan Rites, Xianqing Rites, and the sacrificial code omit gaosu because no age transmitted it—the text was lost. Each omission has its cause; none can serve as proof.

sentences.zh: 今禮官引為明證，在臣誠實有疑。

translations.literal: Now ritual officials cite it as clear proof—in your servant's heart there is real doubt.
translations.idiomatic: The ritualists now cite these as clear proof. Your servant is not persuaded.

sentences.zh: 陛下肇建明堂，聿遵古典，告朔之禮，猶闕舊間，欽若稽古，應須補葺。

translations.literal: Your Majesty newly built the Bright Hall and follows the classics—yet the gaosu rite still lacks in the old interval; reverently examining antiquity, it ought to be repaired.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has raised the Bright Hall and follows the ancients—yet gaosu still stands incomplete. To honor antiquity, the gap should be mended.

sentences.zh: 若每月聽政於明堂，事亦煩數，孟月視朔，恐不可廢。

translations.literal: If each month hearing government at the Bright Hall, the affair is also numerous; viewing the new moon in the first month of each season—fear it cannot be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly audiences at the Bright Hall would be burdensome—but viewing the new moon in each season's first month must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 上又命奉常廣集眾儒，取方慶、仁諝所奏，議定得失。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered the Director of Sacrifices broadly to assemble scholars, taking Fang Qing's and Ren Xu's memorials to debate right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered the Director of Sacrifices to gather scholars and weigh Fang Qing's and Ren Xu's memorials.

sentences.zh: 當時大儒成均博士吳揚吾、太學博士郭山惲曰：「臣等謹按《周禮》、《禮記》及《三傳》，皆有天子告朔之禮。

translations.literal: At the time great scholars Chengjun Erudite Wu Yangwu and Imperial University Erudite Guo Shanyun said: "We respectfully peruse the Rites of Zhou, Record of Rites, and Three Commentaries—all have the Son of Heaven's gaosu rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengjun erudite Wu Yangwu and Imperial University erudite Guo Shanyun said: "We have examined the Rites of Zhou, the Record of Rites, and the Three Commentaries—all attest the Son of Heaven's gaosu rite.

sentences.zh: 夫天子頒告朔于諸侯，秦政焚滅《詩》、《書》，由是告朔禮廢。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued gaosu to the feudal lords; Qin's government burned the Odes and Documents—thereby the gaosu rite was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven proclaimed gaosu to the feudal lords. Qin burned the Odes and Documents—and gaosu perished.

sentences.zh: 今明堂肇建，總章新立，紹百王之絕軌，樹萬代之鴻規，上以嚴配祖宗，下以敬授人時，使人知禮樂，道適中和，災害不生，禍亂不作。

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall is newly built, Total Splendor newly erected, continuing the severed tracks of a hundred kings, planting a great measure for ten thousand generations—above to solemnly consort with ancestors and forbears, below to respectfully grant the human seasons, causing people to know ritual and music, the Way fitting central harmony, disasters not arising, calamity and rebellion not occurring.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall rises anew, Total Splendor freshly founded—reviving the broken line of a hundred kings, planting a measure for ten thousand generations. Above, ancestors are solemnly matched; below, the seasons are reverently granted. Let the people know ritual and music; let the Way hold the center—then disasters will not arise and rebellion will not stir.

sentences.zh: 今若因循頒朔，每月依行，禮貴隨時，事須沿革。

translations.literal: Now if we follow precedent in issuing the new moon each month and execute monthly, ritual values timeliness and affairs require reform.
translations.idiomatic: To issue the calendar every month by rote is not timely. Ritual follows the season; affairs must be adapted.

sentences.zh: 望依王方慶議，用四時孟月日及季夏於明堂修復告朔之禮，以頒天下。

translations.literal: We hope to follow Wang Fangqing's proposal: use the first-month days of the four seasons and the last month of summer at the Bright Hall to restore the gaosu rite and issue it to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We ask to follow Wang Fangqing: on the first days of the four seasons and in the last month of summer, restore gaosu at the Bright Hall and proclaim it to the realm.

sentences.zh: 其帝及神，亦請依方慶用鄭玄義，告五時帝於明堂上。

translations.literal: For Thearchs and spirits too, request following Fangqing in using Zheng Xuan's meaning—announce to the five-season Thearchs atop the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: For Thearchs and spirits as well, follow Fangqing and Zheng Xuan: announce to the five-season Thearchs upon the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 則嚴配之道，通於神明；

translations.literal: Then the way of solemn consort reaches the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: Then the way of solemn matching reaches the spirits;

sentences.zh: 至孝之德，光于四海。

translations.literal: utmost filial virtue radiates over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: utmost filial virtue shines across the four seas.

sentences.zh: 」制從之。

translations.literal: The regulation assented.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 長安四年，始制：「元日明堂受悲，停讀時令。

translations.literal: In Chang'an year 4 a regulation was first made: "On the first day at the Bright Hall receive bei (received text), cease reading seasonal ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chang'an a rule was set: on New Year's Day the Bright Hall received the new moon; reading the seasonal ordinances ceased.

sentences.zh: 」中宗即位，神龍元年九月，親享明堂，合祭天地，以高宗配。

translations.literal: Zhongzong succeeded; ninth month Shenlong year 1, personally enjoyed the Bright Hall, combined sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with Gaozong as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong took the throne. In the ninth month of Shenlong year 1 he personally sacrificed at the Bright Hall, joining Heaven and Earth with Gaozong as consort.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，曲赦京師。

translations.literal: When rites concluded, partial amnesty in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, the capital received a partial amnesty.

sentences.zh: 明年駕入京，于季秋大享，復就圓丘行事，迄于睿宗之世。

translations.literal: Next year the carriage entered the capital; in autumn's last month great sacrifice, again performed at the Round Mound—through Ruizong's age.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the court returned to the capital. The autumn great sacrifice was again held at the Round Mound—so it remained through Ruizong's reign.

sentences.zh: 開元二年八月，太子賓客薛謙光獻《九鼎銘》。

translations.literal: Kaiyuan year 2, eighth month, Crown Prince Guest-friend Xue Qianguang presented Inscriptions on the Nine Cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 2, eighth month: the crown prince's guest-friend Xue Qianguang presented Inscriptions on the Nine Cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 其《蔡州鼎銘》，天后禦撰，曰：「羲、農首出，軒、昊膺期。

translations.literal: The Cauldron Inscription for Caizhou, personally composed by the Heavenly Empress, says: "Xi and Nong first emerged; Xuan and Hao accepted the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Caizhou cauldron inscription, composed by the Heavenly Empress, reads: "Xi and Nong came first; Xuan and Hao took up the mandate.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞繼踵，湯、禹乘時。

translations.literal: Tang and Yu succeeded in turn; Cheng Tang and Yu seized the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Yu followed in turn; Cheng Tang and Yu rode the hour.

sentences.zh: 天地光宅，域中雍熙。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth shone with dwelling; within the realm, harmony flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth were luminous; the realm knew peace.

sentences.zh: 上天降鑒，方建隆基。

translations.literal: Heaven above sent down the mirror; then was Great Prosperity raised.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven sent down its sign—and Great Prosperity was founded.

sentences.zh: 」紫微令姚崇奏曰：「聖人啟運，休兆必彰。

translations.literal: " Director of the Purple Forbidden Yao Chong memorialized: "When the sage begins his fortune, auspicious omens must appear.
translations.idiomatic: " Yao Chong, director of the Purple Forbidden, memorialized: "When a sage opens his fortune, auspicious signs must show.

sentences.zh: 請宣付史館。

translations.literal: We request it be proclaimed to the Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that this be sent to the Historiography.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，幸東都，將行大享之禮。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, favored the eastern capital, about to perform the great sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, first month, the emperor went to the eastern capital to perform the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿王仁忠、博士馮宗陳貞節等議，以武氏所造明堂，有乖典制，奏議曰：

translations.literal: Director of Sacrifices Associate Wang Renzhong, Erudites Feng Zong and Chen Zhenjie, etc. debated that the Bright Hall the Wu clan built violated the canon, memorializing:
translations.idiomatic: Director of Sacrifices associate Wang Renzhong and erudites Feng Zong and Chen Zhenjie argued that the Wu clan's Bright Hall violated the canon. Their memorial said:

sentences.zh: 明堂之建，其所從來遠矣！

translations.literal: The building of the Bright Hall—its origin is far!
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall's origin lies deep in antiquity!

sentences.zh: 自天垂象，聖人則之。

translations.literal: From Heaven's hanging images the sage took his model.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven hung forth its signs; the sage took them as his model.

sentences.zh: 蒿柱茅簷之規，上圓下方之制，考之大數，不逾三七之間，定之方中，必居丙巳之地者，豈非得房心布政之所，當太微上帝之宮乎？

translations.literal: Artemisia pillars and thatch eaves in plan, round above and square below in form—examining the great numbers, not exceeding the interval of three and seven; fixing it at the center of the square, it must occupy the land of bing and si—is this not obtaining the place where the Heart of the Room deploys government, facing the Supreme Palace of the High God?
translations.idiomatic: Artemisia pillars, thatch eaves—round above, square below. By great number it does not exceed three-sevenths; fixed at the square's center it must sit in bing-si—is this not the Heart of the Room where policy is proclaimed, the Supreme Palace of the High God?

sentences.zh: 故仰葉俯從，正名定位，人神不雜，各司其序，則嘉應響至，保合太和。

translations.literal: Thus looking up to the leaf and bowing to the follower, rectifying names and fixing positions, human and spirit not mixed, each keeping its order—then auspicious responses sound forth and great harmony is preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven above, earth below—names rectified, positions fixed. Human and spirit do not mingle; each keeps its order. Then auspicious omens answer and great harmony holds.

sentences.zh: 昔漢氏承秦，經籍道息，旁求湮墜，詳究難明。

translations.literal: Formerly Han inherited Qin; the classics' Way ceased; seeking what was drowned and lost, detailed investigation was hard to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited Qin; the classics' Way went dark. What was drowned could barely be recovered; the details could not be made clear.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，議立明堂于長安城南，遭竇太后不好儒術，事乃中廢。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor Wu's reign they debated building a Bright Hall south of Chang'an city; they met Empress Dowager Dou's dislike of Ruist learning—the affair was abandoned midway.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Wu's reign they debated a Bright Hall south of Chang'an. Empress Dowager Dou despised Ruist learning—the work stopped midway.

sentences.zh: 孝成之代，又欲立于城南，議其制度，莫之能決。

translations.literal: In Emperor Cheng's age they again wished to build south of the city; debating its institution, none could decide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng they wished again to build south of the city. On the design none could agree.

sentences.zh: 至孝平元始四年，始創造於南郊，以申嚴配。

translations.literal: By Emperor Ping's Yuanshi year 4 they first created it at the southern suburb to extend solemn consort.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Yuanshi year 4 of Emperor Ping was it first built at the southern suburb, for solemn matching.

sentences.zh: 光武中元元年，立于國城之南。

translations.literal: Guangwu, Zhongyuan year 1, built it south of the capital walls.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu, Zhongyuan year 1: it stood south of the capital walls.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉迄于梁朝，雖規制或殊，而所居之地，常取丙巳者，斯蓋百王不易之道也。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin down to the Liang court, though regulations differed, the place occupied always took bing-si—this is the Way a hundred kings do not change.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin through Liang, forms differed—but the site always lay in bing-si. That is the Way no king changes.

sentences.zh: 高宗天皇大帝纂承平之運，崇樸素之風，四夷來賓，九有鹹乂。

translations.literal: High Ancestor the Heavenly August Emperor succeeded the age of peace, honored plain and simple winds; the four barbarians came as guests; the nine regions all were governed.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor the Heavenly August Emperor inherited an age of peace and honored simplicity. The four quarters came as guests; the nine regions were governed.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，詔禮官學士議明堂制度，群儒紛競，各執異端，久之不決，因而遂止者，何也？

translations.literal: Yonghui year 3, an edict ordered ritual officials and scholars to debate Bright Hall institutions; the Ruists disputed, each holding a different extreme; long unable to decide—thereupon it stopped. Why?
translations.idiomatic: Yonghui year 3: ritualists and scholars were ordered to debate the Bright Hall. The Ruists quarreled; each clung to his view; no decision came—and the work halted. Why?

sentences.zh: 非謂財不足、力不堪也。

translations.literal: It was not that funds were insufficient or strength inadequate.
translations.idiomatic: Not for lack of money or strength.

sentences.zh: 將以周、孔既遙，禮經且紊，事不師古，或爽天心，難用作程，神不孚祐者也。

translations.literal: It was because Zhou and Confucius were already distant, the ritual classics already tangled; affairs not taking antiquity as teacher perhaps offended Heaven's heart; hard to use as measure; the spirits did not sincerely bless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Confucius were far; the ritual classics were tangled. What did not follow antiquity might offend Heaven; what could not serve as standard lacked the spirits' blessing.

sentences.zh: 則天太后總禁闈之政，藉軒台之威，屬皇室中圮之期，躡和熹從權之制。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Empress Dowager held the inner court's government, borrowed the Terrace Pavilion's authority, stood in the imperial house's mid-collapse, trod He and Xi's expedient institutions.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Empress Dowager ruled the inner court, drew on the Terrace Pavilion's power, stood in the house's collapse, and walked He and Xi's path of expedience.

sentences.zh: 以為乾元大殿，承慶小寢，當正陽亭午之地，實先聖聽斷之宮。

translations.literal: She held that the Qianyuan great hall and Chengqing lesser chambers occupied the place of upright yang and noon—the very palace where the sage listened and judged.
translations.idiomatic: She held that the Qianyuan great hall and Chengqing chambers sat where yang stood upright at noon—the very hall of the sage's judgment.

sentences.zh: 表順端闈，儲精營室，爰從朝享，未始臨禦。

translations.literal: Manifesting compliance at the correct gate, storing essence in the Encampment chamber—from morning sacrifice she had never yet faced the court.
translations.idiomatic: She marked compliance at the correct gate and stored essence in the Encampment—yet from morning rites she never held court there.

sentences.zh: 乃起工徒，挽令摧覆。

translations.literal: Then she raised workers and laborers and ordered them to pull it down and overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: She raised laborers and had it pulled down.

sentences.zh: 既毀之後，雷聲隱然，眾庶聞之，或以為神靈感動之象也。

translations.literal: After it was destroyed thunder sounded faintly; the multitude heard it—some took it as an image of spiritual powers moved.
translations.idiomatic: After the destruction thunder murmured; the crowd heard it—some said the spirits had been stirred.

sentences.zh: 於是增土木之麗，因府庫之饒，南街北闕，建天樞大儀之制；

translations.literal: Thereupon she increased timber and earth's splendor, relied on the treasury's abundance—south street and north gate, building the Heavenly Pivot and Great Instrument forms;
translations.idiomatic: Then she piled timber and earth into splendor, drawing on full treasuries—south street, north gate, the Heavenly Pivot and Great Instrument;

sentences.zh: 乾元遺趾，興重閣層樓之業。

translations.literal: on the Qianyuan ruins she raised the work of stacked pavilions and layered towers.
translations.idiomatic: on Qianyuan's ruins, towers upon towers.

sentences.zh: 煙焰蔽日，樑柱排雲，人斯告勞，天實貽誡。

translations.literal: Smoke and flame veiled the sun; beams and pillars ranked with clouds; men cried out in toil; Heaven truly sent warning.
translations.idiomatic: Smoke veiled the sun; beams pierced the clouds. Men groaned under the labor; Heaven sent its warning.

sentences.zh: 煨燼甫爾，遽加修復。

translations.literal: Hardly were the embers warm when repair was hastily added.
translations.idiomatic: The ashes were barely cool when rebuilding began.

sentences.zh: 況乎地殊丙巳，未答靈心，跡匪膺期，乃申嚴配。

translations.literal: Moreover the land differed from bing-si, not answering the spirits' heart; the trace did not match the mandate—yet solemn consort was extended.
translations.idiomatic: Worse: the site was not bing-si—it did not answer the spirits. The footprint did not match the mandate—yet solemn matching was performed.

sentences.zh: 事昧彝典，神不昭格。

translations.literal: The affair was obscure to the constant canon; the spirits did not brightly descend.
translations.idiomatic: The rite strayed from the canon; the spirits did not descend.

sentences.zh: 此其不可者一也。

translations.literal: This is the first thing that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first impossibility.

sentences.zh: 又明堂之制，木不鏤，土不文。

translations.literal: Again, Bright Hall's institution: wood is not carved, earth is not patterned.
translations.idiomatic: Again: Bright Hall wood is not carved, earth is not patterned.

sentences.zh: 今體式乖宜，違經紊禮，雕鐫所及，窮侈極麗。

translations.literal: Now the form and style are improper, violating the classics and tangling ritual—where carving reaches, extravagance is exhausted to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Today the form is wrong, the classics violated, ritual tangled—carving pushed to the furthest excess.

sentences.zh: 此其不可者二也。

translations.literal: This is the second thing that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second impossibility.

sentences.zh: 高明爽塏，事資虔敬，密邇宮掖，何以祈天？

translations.literal: Lofty, bright, open and high—the affair relies on reverent respect; closely neighboring the palace quarters—how pray to Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Bright Hall must be lofty, open, and pure—fit for reverence. Pressed against the palace quarters—how does one pray to Heaven?

sentences.zh: 人神雜擾，不可放物。

translations.literal: Human and spirit mixed and disturbed—cannot release the vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Human and spirit mingle; the vessels cannot be set forth properly.

sentences.zh: 此其不可者三也。

translations.literal: This is the third thing that cannot be.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third impossibility.

sentences.zh: 況兩京上都，萬方取則，而天子闕當陽之位，聽政居便殿之中，職司其憂，豈容沉默。

translations.literal: Moreover the two capitals are the upper capitals; the ten thousand directions take them as model—yet the Son of Heaven lacks the position of facing yang, hearing government in the convenient hall's interior; the offices responsible ought to worry—how can they remain silent?
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals are models for the realm—yet the Son of Heaven lacks the seat facing the sun and holds court in a side hall. Those charged with duty cannot keep silent.

sentences.zh: 當須審考曆之計，擇煩省之宜，不便者量事改修，可因者隨宜適用，削彼明堂之號，克復乾元之名，則當寧無偏，人識其舊矣。

translations.literal: One must carefully examine calendrical plans, choose what is troublesome to reduce; what is inconvenient measure the affair and revise; what can be followed adapt as fit; cut that Bright Hall title, restore the Qianyuan name—then the throne will not be partial and people will know the old.
translations.idiomatic: Examine the calendar, choose what may be simplified; revise what fails; keep what serves. Strip the name Bright Hall, restore Qianyuan—then the throne is not skewed and the people recognize what was.

sentences.zh: 詔令所司詳議奏聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to debate in detail and memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the offices to debate and report.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書王志愔等奏議，鹹以此堂所置，實乖典制，多請改削，依舊造乾元殿。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Wang Zhiyin and others memorialized—all held that where this hall was placed truly violated the canon; many requested alteration and cutting, following the old in building Qianyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Justice Wang Zhiyin and others agreed the hall's placement violated the canon. Most asked that it be cut back and Qianyuan Hall rebuilt as of old.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「古之操插皇綱、執大象者，何嘗不上稽天道，下順人極，或變通以隨時，爰損益以成務。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued: "Those of old who grasped the imperial net and held the great image—when did they not above examine Heaven's Way and below comply with man's pole, or change and extend according to the time, or decrease and increase to accomplish the task?
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Those who held the imperial net and grasped the great image—when did they not look up to Heaven's Way and down to man's pole, change with the times, and trim or add to finish the work?

sentences.zh: 且衢室創制，度堂以筵，用之以禮神，是光孝享，用之以布政，蓋稱視朔，先王所以厚人倫、感天地者也。

translations.literal: Moreover the Crossroads Chamber's creation measured the hall by mats; using it to sacrifice to spirits is to glorify filial sacrifice; using it to deploy government is called viewing the new moon—the former kings' means to thicken human relations and move Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Crossroads Chamber was measured in mats: for spirits it glorified sacrifice; for government it was called viewing the new moon—the former kings' way of thickening human ties and moving Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 少陽有位，上帝斯歆，此則神貴於不黷，禮殷於至敬。

translations.literal: Lesser yang has its position; the High God then rejoices—this is spirits valued in not being profaned, ritual enriched in utmost respect.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser yang has its station; the High God delights—spirits are not profaned; ritual reaches utmost respect.

sentences.zh: 今之明堂，俯鄰宮掖，此之嚴祀，有異肅恭，苟非憲章，將何軌物？

translations.literal: Now's Bright Hall leans neighbor to the palace quarters—this solemn sacrifice differs from solemn respect; if not the constitution and statutes, what will regulate things?
translations.idiomatic: Today's Bright Hall leans on the palace—this solemn rite is not solemnly performed. Without the statutes, what will the realm follow?

sentences.zh: 由是禮官博士、公卿大夫，廣參群議，欽若前古，宜存露寢之式，用罷辟雍之號。

translations.literal: Hence ritual officials, erudites, and grandees broadly joined the many deliberations, reverently like the former ancients—it is fit to preserve the dew-chamber form and abolish the Imperial Academy title.
translations.idiomatic: Ritualists, erudites, and grandees deliberated and, reverencing antiquity, held that the dew-chamber form should remain and the Imperial Academy title be dropped.

sentences.zh: 可改為乾元殿，每臨禦宜依正殿禮。

translations.literal: It may be changed to Qianyuan Hall; whenever facing the court it should follow main-hall ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Let it be renamed Qianyuan Hall; audiences shall follow main-hall ritual.

sentences.zh: 」自是駕在東都，常以元日冬至於乾元殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: " From this when the carriage was at the eastern capital, it regularly on New Year's Day and winter solstice received court congratulations at Qianyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Henceforth at the eastern capital, New Year's Day and the winter solstice brought court congratulations at Qianyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 季秋大享祀，依舊於圓丘行事。

translations.literal: The autumn last-month great sacrifice still was performed at the Round Mound as of old.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn great sacrifice was still held at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 十年，復題乾元殿為明堂，而不行享祀之禮。

translations.literal: Year 10, again titled Qianyuan Hall as Bright Hall, but did not perform the sacrifice rite.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Qianyuan Hall was titled Bright Hall again—but no sacrifice was performed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，駕在西京，詔將作大匠康紵素往東都毀之。

translations.literal: Year 25, the carriage at the western capital, edicted Master of Works Kang Yuesu to go to the eastern capital and destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: Year 25: the court was at the western capital and ordered the master of works Kang Yuesu to destroy the eastern structure.

sentences.zh: 紵素以毀拆勞人，乃奏請且拆上層，卑於舊制九十五尺。

translations.literal: Yuesu, because demolition taxed the people, memorialized requesting for the time being only to dismantle the upper story, lower than the old institution by ninety-five chi.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yuesu, seeing that demolition burdened the people, asked to remove only the upper story—ninety-five chi below the old height.

sentences.zh: 又去柱心木，平座上置八角樓，樓上有八龍，騰身捧火珠。

translations.literal: He again removed the pillar-heart timber; on the level terrace he placed an eight-sided tower; atop the tower eight dragons, bodies soaring, bore the fire pearl.
translations.idiomatic: He removed the pillar cores and set an eight-sided tower on the level terrace; eight dragons coiled upward bearing the fire pearl.

sentences.zh: 又小於舊制，周圍五尺，覆以真瓦，取其永逸。

translations.literal: Again smaller than the old institution—circumference five chi, covered with true tile, taking everlasting ease.
translations.idiomatic: It was smaller still than the old measure—five chi around, roofed with true tile for lasting ease.

sentences.zh: 依舊為乾元殿。

translations.literal: Following the old, it was again Qianyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: As of old, it was Qianyuan Hall again.
